accel_to_decel_enable: Enables a firmware cap on deceleration relative to acceleration (Klipper-style accel_to_decel). Smooths velocity changes on short moves, reducing vibration and ringing at slight cost to print time. Cap value set by accel_to_decel_factor.
accel_to_decel_factor: Deceleration cap as percent of print acceleration; active only with accel_to_decel_enable. Lower percent = gentler decelerations, less ringing on short zigzag moves, slower prints. 50% typical; 1-100%.
activate_air_filtration: Per-filament switch for chamber exhaust/air filtration during printing. Enable for fume-emitting materials (ABS, ASA); off for PLA-types where exhaust airflow cools the chamber. Fan level via during_print_exhaust_fan_speed.
additional_cooling_fan_speed: Auxiliary (side) part cooling fan speed, percent. Bulk airflow beyond the hotend fan; helps high-speed PLA/PETG cooling and small features. Keep 0 for warp-prone materials (ABS/ASA/PA) needing a warm chamber. Per-filament.
additional_fan_full_speed_layer: Layer index at which the auxiliary cooling fan reaches its configured speed; below it the fan ramps up or stays off to protect first-layer adhesion. 0 disables the delay. Works alongside close_additional_fan_first_x_layers.
apply_scarf_seam_on_circles: Applies scarf (gradually blended) seams on circular contours handled by circle compensation, hiding the seam bump on holes and cylinders. Disable only if scarf seams cause artifacts; requires scarf seam mode active.
auxiliary_fan: Declares that the machine has an auxiliary (side) part-cooling fan, enabling the filament and process keys that drive it.
avoid_crossing_wall_includes_support: Extends avoid-crossing-wall travel routing to treat support structures as obstacles too. Reduces stringing and scars across supports at the cost of longer travel moves and slicing time. Only relevant when avoid crossing walls is on.
bed_custom_model: Path to a 3D model used to draw the bed in the scene. Cosmetic; no effect on slicing.
bed_custom_texture: Path to an image drawn on the bed surface in the 3D scene. Cosmetic; no effect on slicing.
bed_exclude_area: Bed regions objects may not occupy, as 'XxY' polygon points. Covers fixed hardware such as a purge chute or nozzle wiper. Empty when the whole bed is usable.
bed_temperature_formula: How the bed target is chosen when several filaments print together. by_first_filament takes the first filament's bed temperature; by_highest_temp takes the highest requested — safer for adhesion, riskier for low-temperature materials.
before_layer_change_gcode: Custom g-code emitted just before the Z move that starts a layer. Placeholders such as [layer_num] and [layer_z] expand. Runs earlier than layer_change_gcode.
best_object_pos: Preferred object placement as bed fractions, 'XxY' in 0-1. Studio centres a single object here; useful when part of the bed is flatter or better cooled.
bottom_color_penetration_layers: For multi-color painted models: number of layers the bottom-surface paint color extends upward into the part. More layers keep color visible after sanding or with translucent filament but raise filament change count. 3 typical.
bottom_shell_layers: Solid layers closing the part underside. More = stronger, more watertight bottom, more material/time; 0 leaves infill exposed. Effective thickness is max of this and bottom_shell_thickness. 3-4 typical.
bottom_shell_thickness: Minimum bottom solid thickness in mm; slicer adds bottom layers beyond bottom_shell_layers until this is met. Keeps bottom strength constant across layer heights. 0 = layer count alone governs.
bottom_surface_density: Fill density of bottom solid surfaces, percent. Below 100% leaves micro-gaps: saves material and can improve bridging over infill, but sacrifices watertightness and finish. Keep 100 unless deliberately lightening hidden undersides. 10-100%.
bottom_surface_pattern: Pattern for bottom solid surfaces. concentric: contour rings; zig-zag: fast lines; monotonic: single sweep direction, best for visible undersides; monotonicline: monotonic, connected ends; alignedrectilinear: fixed line angle; hilbertcurve/archimedeanchords/octagramspiral: decorative.
bridge_angle: Forces bridging line direction in degrees; 0 = automatic per-bridge detection. Set manually when auto direction picks long unsupported spans; lines should run the shortest distance between anchored edges. Rarely changed from 0.
bridge_flow: Extrusion flow multiplier for bridge lines (0-2, default 1). Below 1 thins and tensions strands, reducing sag on unsupported spans; too low causes gaps and weak bridges. 0.8-0.95 common tuning range.
bridge_no_support: Suppresses support generation under detected bridge regions, trusting bridging settings to span them. Saves material and post-processing; risky for spans beyond the filament's bridging ability. Only matters when supports are enabled.
bridge_speed: Print speed for bridge lines, mm/s. Slow speeds let strands cool and anchor before sagging; too slow can increase drooping with some materials. 20-30 mm/s typical. Pair with high fan and reduced bridge_flow.
brim_object_gap: Clearance between brim and part outline, mm (0-2). Larger gap = easier brim removal, weaker adhesion aid; 0 fuses brim to part for maximum hold but harder cleanup. 0.1 mm is a common compromise.
brim_type: Brim placement. auto_brim: slicer decides per object based on adhesion risk; brim_ears: small discs at sharp corners only; outer_only: brim outside the outline (most common manual choice); inner_only: inside holes only; outer_and_inner: both sides; no_brim: none. Outer brims fight warping; inner brims consume hole clearance.
brim_width: Brim width in mm (0-100), used when brim_type is not auto. Wider brim = more bed grip against warping and tipping, more material and cleanup. 3-8 mm covers most cases; tall thin parts benefit from more.
chamber_temperatures: Target chamber temperature, C (0-80, 0 = uncontrolled). Warm chamber cuts warping and boosts layer adhesion for ABS/ASA/PA/PC; keep 0 for PLA/PETG to avoid heat creep. Only honored by printers with chamber control.
change_filament_gcode: G-code emitted at each filament change to unload, purge, and load the next filament. Placeholders identify the outgoing and incoming filaments.
circle_compensation_manual_offset: Extra user diameter offset, mm, added on top of automatic circular hole compensation. Positive enlarges compensated holes, negative shrinks. Use after measuring printed test holes; 0 leaves the model-based compensation unchanged.
circle_compensation_speed: Calibration reference speed, mm/s, the circular contour compensation model assumes for this filament; does not command actual print speed. Change only when recalibrating compensation coefficients with new test prints.
close_additional_fan_first_x_layers: Number of initial layers with the auxiliary cooling fan forced off. Protects first-layer adhesion and reduces warping at the base. 1-3 typical; raise for warp-prone materials.
close_fan_the_first_x_layers: Number of initial layers with the part cooling fan forced off. Ensures hot, well-bonded first layers on the bed; too many fanless layers can hurt small overhangs near the base. 1 typical for PLA, 3+ for ABS/ASA.
compatible_printers: List of printer profile names this preset applies to. Empty = compatible with all. Metadata for preset filtering, not print behavior.
compatible_printers_condition: Boolean expression over printer config values (e.g. nozzle_diameter, printer_model) gating whether this preset is offered for a printer. Empty = always compatible. Metadata, no print effect.
compatible_prints: List of process (print) profile names this filament preset applies to. Empty = all. Metadata for preset filtering.
compatible_prints_condition: Boolean expression over process config values gating whether this filament preset is offered with a given process profile. Empty = always. Metadata, no print effect.
complete_print_exhaust_fan_speed: Exhaust fan speed, percent, run after the print finishes to purge chamber fumes. Higher clears VOCs faster; mainly for ABS/ASA and other fume-heavy materials. Needs air filtration hardware. 80 typical.
cool_plate_temp: Bed temperature, C, for layers after the first on the Cool Plate build surface. Plate-specific counterpart to hot/textured/engineering plate temps. 35 C typical for PLA; exceeding the plate's rating degrades its coating.
cool_plate_temp_initial_layer: First-layer bed temperature, C, on the Cool Plate surface. Slightly higher than later layers can aid adhesion; Cool Plate is designed for low-temp printing (PLA), so values stay near 35 C.
cooling_filter_enabled: Runs the machine's cooling filter while printing. Requires support_cooling_filter.
cooling_perimeter_transition_distance: Distance, mm, over which fan speed blends when perimeters enter/leave regions needing different cooling (e.g. overhangs). Longer = smoother fan ramps, fewer surface marks; shorter = more responsive overhang cooling. 10 mm default.
cooling_slowdown_logic: Strategy used when layer time falls below the cooling threshold: 'uniform_cooling' slows the whole layer evenly, 'consistent_surface' preserves outer-wall speed for a uniform sheen and slows other features harder. Per extruder position.
counter_coef_1: Circular compensation: constant term of the polynomial that predicts inner-hole (counter) diameter shrinkage for this filament. Calibrated per material; edit only with measured hole-test data.
counter_coef_2: Circular compensation: linear term of the inner-hole diameter compensation polynomial for this filament. Scales correction with hole diameter. Calibrated value; change only from hole-test measurements.
counter_coef_3: Circular compensation: additional polynomial term of the inner-hole diameter correction model for this filament. Calibrated per material from test prints.
counter_limit_max: Upper clamp, mm, on the automatic inner-hole/contour diameter correction. Prevents the compensation polynomial from over-enlarging features on out-of-range diameters.
counter_limit_min: Lower clamp, mm, on the automatic inner-hole/contour diameter correction. Prevents the compensation polynomial from over-shrinking features; negative values allow slight reduction.
default_acceleration: Acceleration, mm/s2, for print moves without a feature-specific override. Higher = shorter prints, more ringing/ghosting; lower = cleaner corners. 500 is conservative; modern CoreXY machines run thousands.
default_filament_colour: Display color assigned to this filament in the UI and multi-color previews (hex string). Cosmetic and for AMS slot matching; no effect on toolpaths.
default_filament_profile: Filament preset selected by default for each extruder when this machine is chosen. Per extruder.
default_jerk: Default jerk (instantaneous velocity change) limit, mm/s, for moves lacking a feature-specific jerk. Higher = quicker direction changes and shorter prints but more vibration and corner artifacts; 0 defers to feature/machine values.
default_nozzle_volume_type: Nozzle volume class selected by default for each extruder, such as standard or high flow. Picks which calibrated flow and purge data apply.
default_print_profile: Process preset selected by default when this machine is chosen.
deretraction_speed: Speed (mm/s) at which retracted filament is pushed back, per extruder. 0 reuses retraction_speed. Slower helps flexibles and high-flow hotends recover cleanly.
detect_floating_vertical_shell: Scans vertical shell (wall) paths for segments printed over air and drops them to bridge speed. Prevents wall sag above sparse infill or internal voids. Disable only when the slowdown is unacceptable on known-safe geometry.
detect_narrow_internal_solid_infill: Auto-detects narrow internal solid infill regions and fills them concentrically instead of rectilinear. Fewer direction reversals in tight areas: less shaking, slightly faster. Rarely worth disabling.
detect_overhang_wall: Classifies wall segments by overhang degree so degree-tiered overhang speeds can apply. Prerequisite for enable_overhang_speed to act. Better overhang surfaces at some speed cost; keep on.
detect_thin_wall: Detects walls too narrow for two line widths and prints them as a single extrusion instead of omitting them. Preserves thin features (text, fins); slower slicing, single-line walls are weaker. Default off.
diameter_limit: Per-filament upper bound (mm) for auto circle contour-hole compensation: circular holes/contours above this diameter are left uncorrected. Acts with enable_circle_compensation and the hole limit values. Default 50.
draft_shield: Prints a wall around the model to block drafts and trap heat, reducing warping of high-shrinkage materials. disabled: none; limited: shield only up to skirt height; enabled: full object height. Costs material, time, and plate area.
during_print_exhaust_fan_speed: Exhaust/air-filtration fan speed (%) while printing; overrides speeds set in filament custom G-code. Raise to extract fumes (ABS/ASA); high values drop chamber temperature, so keep low for warp-prone high-temp materials. Default 60.
elefant_foot_compensation: Shrinks first-layer perimeters inward by this many mm to cancel the squish bulge (elephant foot). Restores bottom-edge dimensional accuracy and part fit. Too much undercuts the base and weakens bed adhesion. Typical 0-0.2 mm.
embedding_wall_into_infill: In spots where a wall loop cannot fit, sinks the wall into the adjacent infill region so shell and infill join without a gap. Improves bonding and strength in thin cross-sections. Default off.
enable_arc_fitting: Converts segmented toolpaths into G2/G3 arc moves. Smaller G-code and smoother curved motion; introduces a tiny geometric approximation. Requires firmware arc support. Default off.
enable_circle_compensation: Experimental correction of circular hole and contour diameters for shrinkage, up to the filament's diameter_limit (~50 mm). Only certain filaments supported (PLA Basic/CF, PET CF, PETG CF/HF); manual offset key biases fit tighter/looser.
enable_height_slowdown: Ramps print speed down across a Z range defined by the slowdown start/end height and speed keys. Counters tall-part wobble and resonance on slender models. Nullable per extruder; default off.
enable_long_retraction_when_cut: Enables the long retraction performed when the filament is cut at a change. 0 off, 1 on; depends on the machine having a cutter.
enable_mixed_color_sublayer: Splits layers containing mixed-color (blended) filaments into sub-layers so alternating deposits produce the color-mixing effect. Multi-color prints only; markedly more filament changes and print time. Default off.
enable_overhang_bridge_fan: Forces the part-cooling fan to the overhang fan speed on overhangs and bridges, bypassing layer-time fan logic. Firms up sagging-prone extrusions. Disable for filaments where extra cooling breaks layer adhesion (ABS/ASA/PC).
enable_overhang_speed: Slows wall printing by overhang degree using the tiered overhang speed values; requires detect_overhang_wall. Less sag and curling on overhangs at a print-time cost. Nullable per extruder; keep on.
enable_pre_heating: Starts hotend temperature changes early, using hotend_heating_rate and hotend_cooling_rate, so the nozzle is at target when the change is due. Cuts idle waiting on multi-filament prints.
enable_pressure_advance: Applies the filament's pressure_advance value (linear advance). Sharper corners, less bulge/gap at speed transitions. Manual value replaces the printer's automatic flow-dynamics calibration; calibrate per filament first.
enable_prime_tower: Prints a purge/wipe tower to clean the nozzle and restabilize melt pressure after filament changes; prevents color bleed and blobs in multi-material prints. Costs material, time, plate space. Usually unnecessary single-filament.
enable_support: Master switch for support generation. Style (normal/tree), threshold angle, and interface behavior come from the other support keys. Enables overhangs beyond self-supporting angle; costs material, time, and supported-surface finish.
enable_support_ironing: Irons the top of support interface layers so the model surface resting on supports comes out flatter and smoother. Adds print time; only matters where supports contact visible undersides. Default off.
enable_tower_interface_features: Applies dedicated temperature, pre-extrusion, and purge settings to prime tower interface layers where different materials meet, improving multi-material tool-change quality. Developer-mode; default off.
enable_wrapping_detection: Enables filament clumping detection (material wrapping around the nozzle) for the print, sized by wrapping_detection_layers. Lets the printer catch clumps early and stop before damage. Requires supporting hardware; default off.
enforce_support_layers: Forces support generation on the first N layers regardless of overhang angle, even with enable_support off. Rescue for parts with tiny bed contact or slight base overhangs. 0 disables; small values (2-5) typical.
eng_plate_temp: Bed temperature (deg C) for layers after the first when the Engineering Plate is selected. Per filament. Higher resists warping; too high softens lower layers and worsens elephant foot. 0 disables bed heating for those layers.
eng_plate_temp_initial_layer: First-layer bed temperature (deg C) on the Engineering Plate. Governs initial adhesion; vendor profiles often match the other-layers plate temp. 0 disables heating for the first layer.
ensure_vertical_shell_thickness: Adds solid infill near sloped surfaces to guarantee the configured shell thickness. enabled: full enforcement, watertight, more material/time; partial: reinforces only critical areas; disabled: fastest, risks gaps or pinholes on slopes.
exclude_object: Writes per-object markers into the G-code so a failed object can be skipped on the printer mid-print while the rest continue. Needs firmware/printer support; minor G-code size increase. Keep on for multi-object plates.
extruder_clearance_dist_to_rod: Horizontal clearance (mm) from the nozzle to the gantry rods. Used with the height clearances to space objects printed one at a time.
extruder_clearance_height_to_lid: Vertical clearance (mm) from the nozzle tip to the lid or top frame. Second height limit on object height in sequential printing.
extruder_clearance_height_to_rod: Vertical clearance (mm) from the nozzle tip up to the gantry rods. Caps how tall a finished object may be when the head passes over it in sequential printing.
extruder_clearance_max_radius: Radius (mm) of the toolhead's largest horizontal footprint. Minimum spacing between objects in sequential printing.
extruder_colour: Display colour per extruder as a hex string (#RRGGBB). Preview only; no effect on slicing.
extruder_max_nozzle_count: Nozzles the extruder can carry, per extruder. Above one only on toolheads with switchable nozzles.
extruder_offset: Nozzle offset per extruder as 'XxY' millimetres from the machine origin. Non-zero for a second toolhead; the slicer compensates every move by it.
extruder_printable_area: Per-extruder reachable outline, one entry per extruder, each a comma-joined list of 'XxY' points. Narrows printable_area for a toolhead that cannot cover the whole bed.
extruder_printable_height: Per-extruder maximum Z in mm; a 'nil' column keeps the machine-wide printable_height. Lower for a toolhead mounted higher than its sibling.
extruder_type: Extruder drive layout per extruder. Direct Drive mounts the gears at the hotend and needs short retractions; Bowden pushes through a long tube and needs far longer ones.
extruder_variant_list: Every extruder variant this machine supports, as 'drive type + nozzle volume' strings. printer_extruder_variant picks from this list.
fan_cooling_layer_time: Layer-time threshold (s) for cooling control: layers faster than this get fan speed interpolated from fan_min_speed up toward fan_max_speed; slower layers stay at fan_min_speed. Larger value = fan ramps up on more layers. Default 60.
fan_direction: Side the auxiliary fan blows from. Lets the slicer bias seam and overhang placement relative to the airflow.
fan_max_speed: Part-cooling fan ceiling (%) applied as layer times approach zero; interpolation target above fan_min_speed per fan_cooling_layer_time. High (80-100) for PLA/PETG detail; low for ABS/ASA to protect layer bonding. Per filament.
fan_min_speed: Baseline part-cooling fan speed (%) used on layers longer than fan_cooling_layer_time; effectively the filament's always-on fan level. Moderate for PLA; near 0 for warp-prone ABS/ASA/PC. Per filament.
filament_adaptive_volumetric_speed: Limits extrusion flow to the smaller of a fitted value (from line width and layer height via the volumetric speed coefficients) and the fixed max volumetric speed. Off: fixed max only. Evens quality across mixed line widths.
filament_adhesiveness_category: Developer field: integer class describing how the filament bonds to other materials. Consulted for multi-material pairing decisions such as support/interface suitability. Vendor-set; not user-tuned.
filament_bridge_speed: Per-extruder override of bridge printing speed (mm/s) for this filament; 'nil' keeps the process value. Materials with poor bridging (PETG) want slower bridges with strong cooling; PLA tolerates faster. Typical 20-40 mm/s.
filament_change_length: Filament length (mm) extruded from the outgoing extruder during an extruder change to relieve melt pressure and reduce oozing before the swap. Dual-extruder machines. Default 10; raise if change points leave strings or blobs.
filament_change_length_nc: Filament length (mm) extruded from the outgoing nozzle during a hotend change, so the parked hotend oozes less. Hotend-swap counterpart of filament_change_length. Default 10 mm.
filament_cooling_before_tower: Nozzle temperature drop (deg C) allowed before printing on the prime tower after a filament change; cooler entry reduces sag and stringing of purged material. Developer-mode, per filament, default 10.
filament_cost: Filament price per kilogram. Feeds only the cost estimate shown after slicing; no effect on toolpaths or print behavior.
filament_density: Material density in g/cm3. Used for weight and cost estimates in the slice summary; no effect on toolpaths. Typical: PLA ~1.24, PETG ~1.27, ABS ~1.04.
filament_deretraction_speed: Per-extruder override of the speed for re-priming after retraction (mm/s) for this filament; 'nil' keeps the printer value, 0 means use retraction speed. Slower deretraction helps materials that swell in the melt zone re-prime without blobs.
filament_dev_ams_drying_ams_limitations: Developer metadata: free-form note on AMS model restrictions for this filament's drying profile, consumed by the AMS drying feature. Usually empty; no effect on slicing.
filament_dev_ams_drying_heat_distortion_: Developer metadata: heat-distortion temperature (deg C) of the filament/spool, used as a safety ceiling when AMS drying selects temperatures. 0 = unset; no effect on toolpaths.
filament_dev_ams_drying_temperature: Developer metadata: recommended AMS drying temperature (deg C) for this filament, consumed by the AMS drying feature. 0 = unset; no effect on slicing output.
filament_dev_ams_drying_time: Developer metadata: recommended AMS drying duration for this filament, paired with filament_dev_ams_drying_temperature. 0 = unset; no effect on slicing output.
filament_dev_chamber_drying_bed_temperat: Heatbed temperature (C) for the in-chamber filament drying routine. Higher dries faster but must stay safe for the material; 0 disables. Developer-level setting; pair with filament_dev_chamber_drying_time.
filament_dev_chamber_drying_time: Duration of the in-chamber filament drying routine. Longer removes more moisture; hygroscopic materials (PA, PC, TPU) need extended runs. Developer-level setting used with filament_dev_chamber_drying_bed_temperature.
filament_dev_drying_cooling_temperature: Chamber temperature (C) the printer cools down to after a drying cycle before printing resumes. Prevents feeding filament through an overheated chamber. Developer-level setting; 0 leaves cooldown unmanaged.
filament_dev_drying_softening_temperatur: Material softening temperature (C). Upper safety bound during chamber drying and pre-feed checks: if chamber exceeds it, cooling runs before feeding to avoid soft-filament jams. Set below the temperature where the filament deforms.
filament_diameter: Nominal filament diameter (mm) used to convert extrusion lengths to volume. Wrong value scales all extrusion: too small causes over-extrusion, too large under-extrusion. Measure stock if flow is off. Standard 1.75; some machines 2.85.
filament_enable_overhang_speed: Per-extruder override: apply overhang-ratio-based speed reduction for this filament; 'nil' keeps the process setting. Disable only for materials whose overhang quality is insensitive to speed (some engineering blends) to save time.
filament_end_gcode: G-code emitted when this filament is unloaded or its use ends (per-filament, runs at tool change and print end). Typical uses: reset temperatures, fans, or material-specific machine state. Runs before the next filament's start G-code.
filament_extruder_compatibility: Restricts which extruder may print this filament on dual-extruder machines (H2D-class). Encoded as int: 0 = no restriction, otherwise limits assignment to the compatible unit, e.g. abrasive or high-temp materials on the hardened side.
filament_extruder_variant: Names the extruder/hotend hardware variant each vector entry of this filament profile targets (e.g. Direct Drive Standard). Selects which variant-specific values apply; informational for matching, not a print-quality lever.
filament_flow_ratio: Extrusion multiplier applied to all moves with this filament. Raise for gaps/under-extrusion, lower for blobs, bulging seams, rough top surfaces. Calibrate per material; typical 0.92-1.02 (PLA ~0.98, PETG ~0.95). Max 2.
filament_flush_temp: Nozzle temperature (C) used while flushing this filament on the prime/wipe tower during color change. 0 = use normal print temperature. Lower can reduce stringing of oozy materials; must stay high enough to keep flow reliable.
filament_flush_volumetric_speed: Volumetric rate (mm3/s) for purging this filament during flush on the wipe tower. 0 = use filament max volumetric speed. Lower if flushing causes grinding or clicking; higher shortens multi-color change time.
filament_is_support: Marks this filament as dedicated support material (e.g. Bambu Support W/G, PVA). Slicer then prefers it for support interfaces/body and excludes it from model walls. Enables clean separation without tuning interface gaps.
filament_long_retractions_when_cut: Experimental, per-extruder override: pull the filament far back when the cutter severs it (multi-material), reducing degraded material left in the melt zone; 'nil' keeps the printer setting. Only for materials that tolerate re-melting after long dwell.
filament_max_volumetric_speed: Hard cap on extrusion flow (mm3/s); slicer slows any move that would exceed it. Primary speed limiter per material: too high causes under-extrusion at speed, too low wastes time. Typical: PLA 12-21, PETG 8-14, TPU 3-6, high-flow higher.
filament_metal_stickiness: Stickiness class of a metal-fill material (None/Low/Medium/High), used to adapt handling of tacky metal-loaded filaments. Leave None for ordinary polymers.
filament_minimal_purge_on_wipe_tower: Minimum volume (mm3) purged on the wipe tower when switching TO this filament, regardless of computed flush volume. Guards against undersized flush matrices leaving old color/material in the nozzle. Default 15.
filament_notes: Free-text notes stored with the filament profile. No effect on slicing. Use for calibration results (flow, K-factor), drying history, vendor batch info.
filament_overhang_1_4_speed: Per-extruder override of print speed (mm/s) for lines overhanging up to 25% of their width; 'nil' or 0 keeps the process value. First tier of the four-step overhang slowdown ladder for this filament.
filament_overhang_2_4_speed: Per-extruder override of print speed (mm/s) for 25-50% overhanging lines; 'nil' or 0 keeps the process value. Second tier of the overhang slowdown ladder for this filament.
filament_overhang_3_4_speed: Per-extruder override of print speed (mm/s) for 50-75% overhanging lines; 'nil' or 0 keeps the process value. Third tier; heat-sensitive materials benefit most from slowing here.
filament_overhang_4_4_speed: Per-extruder override of print speed (mm/s) for 75-100% overhanging lines; 'nil' or 0 keeps the process value. Steepest supported overhangs; slowest tier before bridging rules apply.
filament_overhang_totally_speed: Per-extruder override of print speed (mm/s) for fully unsupported (100% overhang) lines; 'nil' keeps the process value. Effectively near-bridge printing; keep slow (default 10) with maximum cooling.
filament_pre_cooling_temperature: Target nozzle temperature (C) to start cooling toward during ramming before an extruder change (dual-extruder machines). Issues cool command plus fan only; target not guaranteed. 0 disables. Reduces ooze from the parked tool.
filament_pre_cooling_temperature_nc: Target nozzle temperature (C) to start cooling toward during ramming before a hotend change (dual-nozzle machines). Cooling command plus fan only; target may not be reached before the switch. 0 disables. Cuts ooze from the idle hotend.
filament_preheat_temperature_delta: Offset (C) applied when preheating this filament's nozzle ahead of a toolchange on dual-extruder machines. Negative holds the waiting nozzle cooler to limit ooze/degradation; 0 preheats straight to print temperature.
filament_prime_volume: Volume (mm3) primed on the wipe tower after a filament change to restore steady flow before printing resumes. Raise if first extrusions after a swap are thin or discolored; lower to save material. Default 45.
filament_prime_volume_nc: Volume (mm3) primed on the wipe tower after a hotend change (dual-nozzle machines) before the incoming nozzle prints on the model. More than a plain filament change since the whole melt zone restarts. Default 60.
filament_printable: Bitmask of extruders allowed to print this filament on multi-extruder machines: bit N set = extruder index N permitted; 3 = both. Restrict when a material needs a specific hotend, e.g. hardened nozzle for CF-filled.
filament_ramming_travel_time: Travel dwell (s) after ramming, before an extruder change, letting the filament tip ooze away from the print. 0 disables. Values >0 force wipe-tower ramming line spacing to 2x line width to absorb the overflow. Dual-extruder machines.
filament_ramming_travel_time_nc: Travel dwell (s) after ramming, before a hotend change, giving the retiring nozzle time to ooze off the model. 0 disables. Values >0 widen wipe-tower ramming line spacing to 2x line width. Dual-nozzle machines.
filament_ramming_volumetric_speed: Extrusion rate (mm3/s) for ramming before an extruder change: rapid push shaping a clean filament tip prior to retraction. -1 = automatic (derived from max volumetric speed). Too high grinds filament; too low leaves stringy tips.
filament_ramming_volumetric_speed_nc: Extrusion rate (mm3/s) for ramming before a hotend change on dual-nozzle machines. Shapes the filament tip so the retiring hotend retracts cleanly. -1 = automatic from max volumetric speed. Lower if ramming skips or grinds.
filament_retract_before_wipe: Per-extruder override of how much of the retraction (percent) happens before the wipe move for this filament; 'nil' keeps the printer value. Higher values reduce material available to smear during the wipe; 100% retracts fully first.
filament_retract_length_nc: Retraction length (mm) pulled when this filament's hotend is deactivated during a hotend change. Longer clears the melt zone and stops ooze from the parked nozzle; too long risks jams on re-engage. Range 0-18, default 10.
filament_retract_restart_extra: Per-extruder override of extra filament (mm) extruded when restarting after retraction; 'nil' keeps the printer value. Positive compensates ooze losses on leaky materials; negative counters blobbing. Keep within a few tenths of a millimeter.
filament_retract_when_changing_layer: Per-extruder override: force a retraction on layer change for this filament; 'nil' keeps the printer setting. Enable for materials that leave layer-change blobs; disable to save time with well-behaved filaments.
filament_retraction_distances_when_cut: Per-extruder override of the long-retraction distance (10-18 mm) used when the filament is cut; 'nil' keeps the printer value. Must clear the melt zone without pulling soft filament into the extruder gears.
filament_retraction_length: Per-extruder override of the printer profile's retraction length (mm) for this filament; a 'nil' element keeps the printer value. Flexible and oozy materials often need more than the printer default; direct-drive typically 0.4-1.2 mm, bowden 2-6 mm.
filament_retraction_minimum_travel: Per-extruder override of the minimum travel distance (mm) that triggers a retraction for this filament; 'nil' keeps the printer value. Raise for materials where frequent retracts cause grinding; lower for stringy materials needing retracts even on short hops.
filament_retraction_speed: Per-extruder override of the printer's retraction speed (mm/s) for this filament; 'nil' keeps the printer value. Soft filaments (TPU) need slower retracts to avoid stretching and grinding; rigid materials tolerate fast retracts.
filament_scarf_length: Length (mm) of the scarf joint seam ramp for this filament when scarf seams are enabled. Longer spreads the seam transition, hiding it better on glossy materials; shorter keeps the seam compact. Default 10.
filament_scarf_seam_type: Filament-level scarf seam preference: 'none' keeps ordinary seams, 'external' applies scarf joints to visible outer walls only, 'all' to every wall. Scarf seams ramp the seam over a distance to hide it; effective on glossy materials where seam bumps show most.
filament_shrink: Material shrinkage compensation (%). 100 = no shrinkage; below 100 the slicer scales XY up so cooled parts hit nominal size (e.g. ABS ~99.5, ASA/PA lower). Measure a calibration cube to derive. Affects dimensional accuracy only.
filament_soluble: Marks this filament as dissolvable (PVA, BVOH). Slicer treats it as preferred support/interface material and allows zero interface gaps since it washes out instead of breaking away. Store dry; highly hygroscopic.
filament_start_gcode: G-code emitted when this filament becomes active (print start or tool change, before printing with it). Typical uses: set pressure advance/K-factor, material-specific fans or temperatures. Runs after the previous filament's end G-code.
filament_tower_interface_pre_extrusion_d: Travel distance (mm) covered while pre-extruding before printing a prime tower interface layer with this filament. Spreads the priming line so flow is stable when the interface starts. Works with the pre-extrusion length. Default 10.
filament_tower_interface_pre_extrusion_l: Filament length (mm) pre-extruded before a prime tower interface layer. Primes the nozzle so the interface bonds instead of starting under-extruded; helps towers mixing very different-viscosity materials. 0 disables.
filament_tower_interface_print_temp: Nozzle temperature (C) for printing prime tower interface layers with this filament. -1 = use normal print temperature. Dedicated interface temp improves layer bonding between dissimilar materials and reduces tower collapse.
filament_tower_interface_purge_volume: Purge volume (mm3) flushed when printing a prime tower interface layer with this filament. Ensures the interface is pure material for reliable adhesion between tower sections. Default 20; raise if interfaces delaminate.
filament_tower_ironing_area: Ironing area (mm2) applied on prime tower surfaces for this filament. Flattens the tower top so the next material bonds and the tower stays stable. 0 disables flat ironing (line ironing may remain), improving stability for some materials.
filament_type: Material class string (PLA, PETG, ABS, TPU, PA, PC, PVA...). Drives compatibility checks, flush volume matrix, drying and chamber logic, and default limits. Must match the actual material; not just a label.
filament_velocity_adaptation_factor: Scales how aggressively print velocity adapts for this filament when speed-modulating features engage. 1 = default; lower damps speed changes for materials sensitive to flow transients (TPU, CF-filled).
filament_vendor: Manufacturer name stored in the profile. Identification/metadata only; no slicing effect. Used for profile organization and matching to vendor presets.
filament_wipe: Per-extruder override: wipe the nozzle along the last path while retracting for this filament; 'nil' keeps the printer setting. Effective against ooze marks with PETG and other tacky materials.
filament_wipe_distance: Per-extruder override of the nozzle wipe distance (mm) for this filament; 'nil' keeps the printer value. Longer wipes shear off ooze from stringy materials before travel; too long scars the surface at the seam.
filament_z_hop: Per-extruder override of the printer's Z hop height (mm, 0-5) during retracted travel for this filament; 'nil' keeps the printer value. Raising it fights stringing-prone materials dragging across the part; costs travel time.
filament_z_hop_types: Per-extruder override of the printer's Z hop trajectory for this filament ('Auto Lift', 'Normal Lift', 'Slope Lift', 'Spiral Lift'); 'nil' keeps the printer value. Slope/Spiral reduce stringing and ooze marks on sticky materials by moving diagonally while lifting.
filename_format: Template for exported G-code/3MF filenames. Placeholders in brackets expand at export, e.g. [input_filename_base], plus profile and print-stat variables. No print effect; adjust for organized output naming.
fill_multiline: Number of parallel lines drawn per sparse infill path (1-5). Values >1 print each infill trace as adjacent multi-line bundles, boosting strength/rigidity at the same density pattern with more material and time. 1 = standard single lines.
filter_out_gap_fill: Minimum gap-fill length in mm; shorter gap-fill extrusions are dropped. Raise to suppress stringy micro-fills between walls for cleaner surfaces at slight cost to thin-section strength. 0 keeps all gap fill.
first_x_layer_fan_speed: Auxiliary (chamber-side) cooling fan speed in % applied only during the initial layers. Keep at 0 so early layers cool slowly and bond to the bed. Per-filament vector.
first_x_layer_part_fan_speed: Part cooling fan speed in % during the initial layers; window set by close_fan_the_first_x_layers. 0 disables part cooling there, improving bed adhesion; raise only for severe overhangs starting at layer 1. Per-filament.
flush_into_infill: Purges filament-change waste into sparse infill printed after the change instead of the prime tower. Cuts flush waste; mixed color hidden inside the part. Needs infill still unprinted on that layer to absorb the purge.
flush_into_objects: Purges filament-change waste into the entire body of this object, walls included. Largest waste saving, but color contamination is visible on surfaces; only for parts where appearance is irrelevant.
flush_into_support: Purges filament-change waste into support structures. Default on; supports are discarded, so mixed color costs nothing. Reduces prime tower size and flush volume.
full_fan_speed_layer: Layer at which part cooling fan reaches its target speed; ramps linearly from zero starting after the close_fan_the_first_x_layers window. If set at or below that window, fan jumps straight to full speed. 0 disables the ramp.
fuzzy_skin: Where random wall jitter (rough texture) is applied. none: off, painting still allowed; external: outer contour only, holes stay smooth; all: contour and holes; allwalls: inner walls too; disabled_fuzzy: force off in this region, overriding object setting.
fuzzy_skin_first_layer: Extends fuzzy skin texture onto layer 1. Off keeps the bottom face flat for full bed contact; on gives a uniform texture on all faces but reduces adhesion area.
fuzzy_skin_mode: How texture is produced. displacement: nozzle path jitters sideways; extrusion: path stays straight, flow varies — better dimensional accuracy; combined: both, fills gaps between perimeters. extrusion/combined require fuzzy_skin_thickness <= line width.
fuzzy_skin_noise_type: Texture noise source. classic: uniform random grain; perlin: smooth coherent texture; billow: perlin-like but clumpy/puffy; ridgedmulti: sharp ridges, marble-like; voronoi: surface split into cells, each offset randomly, patchwork look.
fuzzy_skin_octaves: Detail layers for coherent noise (perlin, billow, ridgedmulti). More octaves add finer texture detail and slicing time; classic random noise ignores it. 3-5 typical.
fuzzy_skin_persistence: Amplitude carried into each successive noise octave (0.01-1). Higher keeps fine octaves strong for a rougher, busier texture; lower yields smooth broad features. 0.5 typical.
fuzzy_skin_point_distance: Spacing in mm between jitter points inserted along the wall path. Smaller gives finer grain but much larger G-code and slower printing; larger gives coarse facets. Keep near fuzzy_skin_thickness; 0.8 default.
fuzzy_skin_scale: Base feature size in mm for coherent noise types. Larger values stretch the texture into broad bumps; small values give tight grain. No effect with classic noise.
fuzzy_skin_thickness: Maximum jitter amplitude in mm, the depth of the rough texture. Larger is rougher but hurts dimensional accuracy of outer walls; keep below outer wall line width. extrusion/combined modes require <= line width. 0.3 typical.
gap_infill_speed: Print speed in mm/s for gap fill between walls. These are short zigzag lines; lower speed reduces vibration and blobbing on small features. Nullable per-extruder vector. ~30 mm/s typical.
gcode_add_line_number: Prefixes every G-code line with an Nx line number. Debugging and serial-protocol use only; inflates file size, no print effect.
gcode_flavor: G-code dialect emitted for this machine — marlin and marlin2 for Marlin firmware, klipper for Klipper, reprapfirmware for Duet, and so on. The wrong flavor yields commands the firmware ignores or rejects.
grab_length: Filament length (mm) the extruder gear pulls back to park the tip inside the toolhead when unloading. Per extruder.
group_algo_with_time: Lets the filament-grouping algorithm weigh estimated time alongside material waste when assigning filaments to extruders.
head_wrap_detect_zone: Bed region used by the toolhead wrap-detection routine, as 'XxY' polygon points.
hole_coef_1: Speed term of auto circular-hole compensation: hole offset = coef1*circle_compensation_speed + coef2*diameter + coef3, clamped by hole_limit_min/max. Active only with enable_circle_compensation on supported filaments. Per-filament.
hole_coef_2: Diameter term of auto circular-hole compensation; mm of offset per mm of hole diameter in offset = coef1*speed + coef2*diameter + coef3. Negative default (-0.025) tapers enlargement for bigger holes. Per-filament.
hole_coef_3: Constant term in mm of auto circular-hole compensation formula coef1*speed + coef2*diameter + coef3. Sets the base enlargement applied to detected circular holes. Default 0.28. Per-filament.
hole_limit_max: Upper clamp in mm on the computed circular-hole enlargement from the hole_coef formula. Prevents over-widening small holes. Default 0.25. Per-filament.
hole_limit_min: Lower clamp in mm on the computed circular-hole enlargement from the hole_coef formula. Guarantees a minimum widening so holes never print undersized when compensation is active. Default 0.08. Per-filament.
host_type: Print host software running at print_host — octoprint, prusalink, duet, repetier and friends. Determines which upload API is used.
hot_plate_temp: Bed temperature in C for layers after the first when printing on the Smooth PEI / High Temp plate. Material-dependent: ~45-60 PLA, ~65-80 PETG, ~90-110 ABS/ASA. Too high softens lower layers; too low risks warping. Per-filament.
hot_plate_temp_initial_layer: First-layer bed temperature in C on the Smooth PEI / High Temp plate. Often equal to or 5 C above later layers to maximize adhesion. Per-filament.
hotend_cooling_rate: Hotend cooling rate in °C per second, per extruder. Feeds the pre-heat scheduler so a temperature drop is started early enough.
hotend_heating_rate: Hotend heating rate in °C per second, per extruder. Used with enable_pre_heating to begin heating ahead of the move that needs the new temperature.
impact_strength_z: Filament mechanical-property value for Z-direction (interlayer) impact strength. Development-mode metadata consumed by strength-related features; does not alter sliced geometry. Per-filament.
independent_support_layer_height: Lets supports slice at their own layer heights, decoupled from object layers, enabling custom Z gaps and shorter print time. Invalid when the prime tower is enabled. Disable when interface layers must align exactly with the object.
infill_combination: Prints sparse infill only every few layers at multiplied thickness while walls stay per-layer. Saves significant time; combined height limited by nozzle capability. Best with sturdy patterns; can leave thicker infill visible under thin tops.
infill_direction: Angle in degrees of sparse infill lines relative to X. Most patterns alternate around this base angle per layer. 45 default spreads directional strength; align with expected load for anisotropic parts.
infill_instead_top_bottom_surfaces: Replaces solid top and bottom shells with sparse infill, producing open/porous faces. For filters, lampshades, lightweight cores. Exterior finish and water-tightness are lost.
infill_jerk: Jerk limit in mm/s for infill moves, the allowed instantaneous speed change at direction reversals. Higher keeps speed through zigzags but excites ringing; effective only when jerk/junction control is active. ~9 typical.
infill_lock_depth: Overlap depth in mm where skin and skeleton zones of locked-zag infill interlock. Deeper lock bonds the dense skin layer to the sparse core more strongly at slight material cost. Only meaningful with the locked-zag pattern.
infill_rotate_step: Additional rotation in degrees applied to the infill angle on each successive layer. Nonzero builds a cross-hatched, more isotropic core; 0 keeps the standard fixed/alternating direction. Only some patterns honor it.
infill_shift_step: Lateral offset in mm applied to the infill pattern each layer, weaving zig-zag family patterns into a cross texture across layers. Larger steps coarsen the texture. Default 0.4; 0 stacks lines vertically.
infill_wall_overlap: Overlap of sparse infill into the innermost wall, as % of infill line width. More overlap bonds infill to walls, raising strength; excess causes over-extrusion that can show through outer walls. 10-25% typical.
inherits: Name of the parent system preset this profile derives from. Profile stores only keys that differ; unset keys follow the parent, including after parent updates. Empty means a standalone full profile.
initial_layer_acceleration: Acceleration in mm/s2 for all first-layer moves. Low values place lines gently and precisely, improving bed adhesion; high values risk dragging fresh lines loose. Nullable per-extruder vector. ~300-500 typical.
initial_layer_flow_ratio: Extrusion flow multiplier for the first layer only. Slightly above 1 squishes lines together over uneven beds, closing gaps and boosting adhesion; too high causes ridges the nozzle plows through. 0.9-1.1 typical.
initial_layer_infill_speed: Speed in mm/s for infill areas on the first layer. Can exceed first-layer outline speed since adhesion of interior fill is less critical, but keep moderate to avoid detaching lines. Nullable per-extruder vector. ~60 typical.
initial_layer_jerk: Jerk limit in mm/s for first-layer moves. Low values avoid abrupt direction changes that can shear freshly laid lines off the bed; effective only when jerk control is active. ~9 typical.
initial_layer_line_width: Line width for the first layer, in mm. Wider lines press more plastic onto the plate, improving bed adhesion and tolerance to plate unevenness. Typically 100-150% of nozzle diameter; 0.4-0.5 for a 0.4 nozzle.
initial_layer_print_height: Height of the first layer, in mm. Thicker first layer absorbs bed unevenness and boosts adhesion; thinner sharpens bottom detail but demands better tramming. Independent of layer_height. Typical 0.2, often thicker than remaining layers.
initial_layer_speed: Print speed for all first-layer extrusions except supports, in mm/s. Slower improves squish and bed adhesion; too fast causes detachment and warping. Per-extruder vector; nil entries fall back to defaults. Typical 20-50.
initial_layer_travel_acceleration: Travel-move acceleration on the first layer, in mm/s². Lower reduces jolts that can shift a freshly laid layer or knock loose curled edges. Per-extruder vector. Typical 500-1000, below normal travel acceleration.
inner_wall_acceleration: Acceleration for inner wall extrusions, in mm/s². 0 falls back to default acceleration. Can run higher than outer wall acceleration since inner walls are hidden; raising cuts print time with little visible cost. Per-extruder vector.
inner_wall_jerk: Jerk (instantaneous speed change) for inner wall moves, in mm/s. Higher keeps speed through corners, saving time; lower reduces ringing and mechanical load. Only applies when jerk control is active in the machine profile. Typical 7-12.
inner_wall_line_width: Line width for inner walls, in mm. Wider walls add strength and reduce wall count needed for a given thickness; narrower improves dimensional fit of thin features. Commonly equal to or slightly above nozzle diameter, e.g. 0.4-0.45 for 0.4 nozzle.
inner_wall_speed: Print speed for inner walls, in mm/s. Can exceed outer wall speed since surface finish is hidden; excessive values weaken wall bonding. Per-extruder vector; nil entries fall back to defaults. Typical 1.5-2x outer wall speed.
interface_shells: Forces separate, non-merged shells where different filaments touch in multi-material prints. Improves separation of soluble or breakaway interfaces and keeps translucent materials clean; adds walls, time, and material. Off for ordinary prints.
interlocking_beam: Generates an interlocking beam structure at boundaries between filaments in multi-material prints, mechanically keying materials that bond poorly (e.g. PLA/PETG). Adds slicing time; beam geometry set by the other interlocking_* keys. Off by default.
interlocking_beam_layer_count: Layers per interlocking beam before the beam direction alternates. More layers make coarser, stronger interlocks; fewer make a finer mesh with more material switches. Only used with interlocking_beam enabled. Typical 2.
interlocking_beam_width: Width of each interlocking beam, in mm. Wider beams key materials more strongly but coarsen the boundary zone; narrower beams may be too weak to grip. Only used with interlocking_beam enabled. Typical about 2x line width, e.g. 0.8.
interlocking_boundary_avoidance: Distance from the model's outer surface, in beam widths, kept free of interlocking structure so beams never show through walls. Larger values hide the structure better but shrink the interlocked zone. Only used with interlocking_beam. Typical 2.
interlocking_depth: Distance, in beam widths, that interlocking beams from each material reach into the other. Deeper interlock grips harder but thickens the mixed boundary region. Only used with interlocking_beam enabled. Typical 2.
interlocking_orientation: Rotation angle of the interlocking beam structure in the XY plane, in degrees (0-360). Change to avoid beams aligning with model walls or filament boundaries, which weakens the interlock. Only used with interlocking_beam. Default 22.5.
internal_bridge_support_thickness: Thickness, in mm, of extra dense support layers printed inside sparse infill directly under internal bridges. Raising firms up bridge anchoring and top surfaces over low-density infill at some material cost; 0 disables. Use multiples of layer height, e.g. 0.2.
internal_solid_infill_line_width: Line width for internal solid infill (solid layers below top/above bottom surfaces), in mm. Wider fills faster and bonds shells better; narrower reduces overextrusion artifacts pushing into top surfaces. Typically equal to nozzle diameter or slightly above.
internal_solid_infill_pattern: Pattern for hidden internal solid layers; cosmetics irrelevant. zig-zag/monotonic/monotonicline: fast rectilinear variants; alignedrectilinear: same direction every layer; concentric: follows perimeters; hilbertcurve/archimedeanchords/octagramspiral: slow curves. zig-zag typical.
internal_solid_infill_speed: Print speed for internal solid infill, in mm/s. Hidden surfaces tolerate high speeds; too fast causes underextrusion gaps that weaken solid shells. Per-extruder vector; nil entries fall back to defaults. Usually near or above sparse infill speed; default 100.
ironing_direction: Angle of ironing passes in the XY plane, in degrees (0-360). Rotating relative to top infill direction can hide line artifacts; align with the surface's long axis for fewer turnarounds. Only used when ironing_type enables ironing. Default 45.
ironing_fan_speed: Part cooling fan speed during ironing, percent (0-100). Lower keeps the surface molten longer for better smoothing; higher prevents heat buildup on small tops. -1 leaves fan at the normal setting for the layer. Per-filament vector.
ironing_flow: Extrusion flow during ironing passes, as percent of a normal layer's flow. The small trickle fills scars between top lines; too high piles up ridges and nozzle drag marks, too low leaves lines unsmoothed. Typical 8-15%.
ironing_inset: Distance, in mm, that ironing stays away from the edge of the top surface. Larger inset avoids nozzle rubbing on perimeters and edge blobs but leaves an unironed border. 0 irons up to the wall. Typical 0-0.5.
ironing_pattern: Toolpath pattern for ironing passes. zig-zag: parallel back-and-forth lines, fast, standard choice; concentric: follows the surface outline inward, suits round tops and avoids directional sheen. Only used when ironing is enabled.
ironing_spacing: Spacing between adjacent ironing passes, in mm. Tighter spacing smooths more thoroughly at heavy time cost; wider leaves faint ridges. Typical 0.1-0.2; well below line width so passes overlap.
ironing_speed: Speed of ironing passes, in mm/s. Slower gives the nozzle time to reflow and flatten the surface; faster saves time but smooths less and can skip. Typical 15-30.
ironing_type: Where the hot nozzle re-traverses surfaces to melt them smooth. no ironing: off; top: all upward-facing surfaces; topmost: only each object's highest surface, saving time; solid: every solid layer, mainly to strengthen layer bonding. Adds significant print time.
is_infill_first: Prints sparse infill before walls on each layer. Infill-first gives walls an anchor, improving overhang quality; walls-first gives cleaner, more accurate outer surfaces since infill can't push through. Off (walls first) is the usual choice for appearance.
layer_change_gcode: Custom g-code emitted at the start of each layer, after the Z move. Placeholders such as [layer_num] and [layer_z] expand. See before_layer_change_gcode for the earlier hook.
layer_height: Height of each printed layer, in mm. Lower means finer detail and smoother curves but longer prints; higher means faster with visible stepping. Keep within 25-80% of nozzle diameter; 0.2 standard for 0.4 nozzle.
line_width: Default extrusion line width, in mm, used by any feature without its own width override. Wider improves strength and flow stability; narrower resolves finer detail but risks underextrusion. Typical 100-120% of nozzle diameter.
locked_skeleton_infill_pattern: Pattern for the interior (skeleton) zone when sparse infill uses the Locked Zag pattern. Skeleton bears the load: zig-zag/grid/cubic/gyroid etc. as with normal sparse infill; crosshatch/crosszag suit flexibles. Zig-zag default. Ignored for other infill patterns.
locked_skin_infill_pattern: Pattern for the outer (skin) zone adjacent to walls when sparse infill uses the Locked Zag pattern. Skin zone anchors infill to walls; crosszag default improves wall bonding, other values as with normal sparse infill. Ignored for other infill patterns.
long_retractions_when_cut: Performs the long retraction when the filament is cut, per extruder. Pulls the tip clear of the melt zone so the next filament loads cleanly.
long_retractions_when_ec: Enables an extra-long retraction when the extruder/filament changes, pulling filament far back to cut oozing and cross-contamination during the swap. Slightly slows changes; grinding risk with soft filaments. Per-filament vector; nil falls back to defaults.
machine_end_gcode: G-code appended after the last layer. Typically turns off heaters, retracts, parks the head, and disables motors.
machine_hotend_change_time: Seconds to swap a hotend. Estimation only.
machine_load_filament_time: Seconds the machine needs to load filament. Estimation only; feeds the printing-time prediction for multi-material jobs.
machine_max_acceleration_e: Firmware acceleration cap (mm/s²) for the extruder axis. Governs how sharply retractions can start and stop. A 'nil' column keeps the inherited value.
machine_max_acceleration_extruding: Firmware acceleration cap (mm/s²) for extruding moves. Clamps whatever the process preset requests; raising it past what the frame can take brings ringing and skipped steps. A 'nil' column keeps the inherited value.
machine_max_acceleration_retracting: Firmware acceleration cap (mm/s²) for retraction moves. A 'nil' column keeps the inherited value.
machine_max_acceleration_travel: Firmware acceleration cap (mm/s²) for travel moves — usually the highest of the three, since nothing is being laid down. A 'nil' column keeps the inherited value.
machine_max_acceleration_x: Firmware acceleration cap (mm/s²) for the X axis. Clamps the process preset's accelerations; beyond what the frame tolerates it brings ringing and skipped steps. A 'nil' column keeps the inherited value.
machine_max_acceleration_y: Firmware acceleration cap (mm/s²) for the Y axis. On a bed-slinger this is the axis that moves the print, so it is usually the tighter of X and Y. A 'nil' column keeps the inherited value.
machine_max_acceleration_z: Firmware acceleration cap (mm/s²) for the Z axis. A 'nil' column keeps the inherited value.
machine_max_jerk_e: Firmware jerk limit (mm/s) for the extruder axis. Bounds how abruptly retraction can reverse the filament. A 'nil' column keeps the inherited value.
machine_max_jerk_x: Firmware jerk limit (mm/s) for the X axis — the largest instantaneous speed change allowed at a corner. Higher keeps corners fast but rings; lower is smoother and slower. A 'nil' column keeps the inherited value.
machine_max_jerk_y: Firmware jerk limit (mm/s) for the Y axis: the largest instantaneous speed change allowed at a corner. A 'nil' column keeps the inherited value.
machine_max_jerk_z: Firmware jerk limit (mm/s) for the Z axis. Small, since leadscrews tolerate little abrupt change. A 'nil' column keeps the inherited value.
machine_max_speed_e: Firmware feedrate cap (mm/s) for the extruder axis. Bounds retraction and deretraction speeds however high the extruder keys are set. A 'nil' column keeps the inherited value.
machine_max_speed_x: Firmware feedrate cap (mm/s) for the X axis. Clamps every X move whatever the process preset asks for — a hardware limit, not a tuning knob. A 'nil' column keeps the inherited value.
machine_max_speed_y: Firmware feedrate cap (mm/s) for the Y axis. Clamps every Y move whatever the process preset asks for. A 'nil' column keeps the inherited value.
machine_max_speed_z: Firmware feedrate cap (mm/s) for the Z axis. Far lower than X and Y on leadscrew-driven axes; governs how fast layer changes and z hops move. A 'nil' column keeps the inherited value.
machine_min_extruding_rate: Lowest feedrate (mm/s) the firmware honours while extruding; slower moves are clamped up to it. 0 disables the floor.
machine_min_travel_rate: Lowest feedrate (mm/s) the firmware honours for non-extruding travel. 0 disables the floor.
machine_pause_gcode: G-code emitted where a pause is inserted, usually parking the head and waiting for the operator.
machine_prepare_compensation_time: Seconds of machine preparation — homing, bed levelling, purge — added to the estimated print time ahead of the first layer.
machine_start_gcode: G-code emitted before the first layer: home, heat, level, and purge. Placeholders such as [nozzle_temperature_initial_layer] expand.
machine_switch_extruder_time: Seconds to switch between toolheads on a multi-extruder machine. Estimation only.
machine_unload_filament_time: Seconds the machine needs to unload filament. Estimation only; feeds time prediction for filament changes.
master_extruder_id: Index of the extruder treated as primary. It prints first and supplies the machine-wide defaults.
max_bridge_length: Maximum unsupported internal bridge length, in mm. Internal gaps wider than this get support/dense infill treatment instead of being bridged; raising trusts bridging more and saves material, lowering yields cleaner surfaces over infill. Default 10.
max_layer_height: Largest layer height (mm) the extruder may print, per extruder. 0 means 75% of nozzle_diameter. Caps adaptive and per-object layer heights.
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_nega: Limits how fast volumetric flow may decrease, in mm³/s². Smooths abrupt speed drops so pressure in the nozzle bleeds off gradually, reducing blobs at decelerations. 0 disables. Rarely needed on printers with pressure advance.
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_posi: Limits how fast volumetric flow may increase, in mm³/s². Ramps speed up gradually so nozzle pressure can build, reducing underextrusion after slow sections. 0 disables. Rarely needed on printers with pressure advance.
min_bead_width: Narrowest wall line the Arachne wall generator will emit, as percent of nozzle diameter. Thin geometry below this prints as a single line of at least this width. Lower captures finer walls but risks underextrusion; higher skips fragile beads. Default 85%.
min_feature_size: Smallest model feature the Arachne wall generator will print at all, as percent of nozzle diameter. Features thinner than this are dropped; those between this and min_bead_width widen to a single bead. Lower keeps more fine detail. Default 25%.
min_layer_height: Smallest layer height (mm) the extruder may print, per extruder. Floor for adaptive layer height; 0.07 typical for a 0.4 nozzle.
minimum_sparse_infill_area: Infill regions smaller than this area, in mm², are filled solid instead of sparse. Solid fill in small pockets is stronger and often faster than fiddly sparse paths; raising uses more material. Default 15.
mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth: Depth, in mm, that painted/segmented multi-material regions interleave into each other at their boundary, keying poorly bonding filament pairs together. 0 disables. Deepening strengthens the join but blurs the color boundary inside the part.
mmu_segmented_region_max_width: Caps the width (mm) of a single color-segmentation zone per layer in multi-material painting; wider painted areas split so color boundaries stay geometrically bounded. 0 disables the cap.
monotonic_travel_into_wall: Extends monotonic top/bottom surface lines into the adjacent wall, as percent of line width. Raising closes hairline gaps between surface fill and walls; too high causes overextrusion marks at wall junctions. 0 disables.
no_slow_down_for_cooling_on_outwalls: Exempts outer walls from the automatic layer-time cooling slowdown. Keeps outer wall speed uniform so surface sheen stays consistent; risks sagging on small or short layers since cooling relies on fan alone. Off by default.
nozzle_diameter: Nozzle bore in mm, per extruder. Sets the usable line-width and layer-height range: 0.4 standard, 0.2 for fine detail, 0.6-0.8 for speed and strength.
nozzle_flush_dataset: Index of the calibrated flushing-volume dataset used per extruder. Selects the purge amounts applied at filament changes.
nozzle_height: Height (mm) of the nozzle cone below the hotend body. Sets how close to a finished wall the head may travel without the heatsink striking it.
nozzle_temperature: Nozzle temperature (°C) for all layers after the first. Higher improves layer bonding and flow at speed but increases stringing and sag; lower sharpens detail, risks underextrusion. Stay within the filament's stated temp range.
nozzle_temperature_initial_layer: Nozzle temperature (°C) for the first layer only. A common tuning pattern raises it slightly above other layers for bed adhesion; default equals the other-layer temp. Works with bed temperature and first-layer speed.
nozzle_temperature_range_high: Upper bound (°C) of the filament's usable nozzle temperature range. Slicer warns when configured nozzle temps exceed it. Set from manufacturer spec; printing above risks degradation, stringing, heat creep.
nozzle_temperature_range_low: Lower bound (°C) of the filament's usable nozzle temperature range. Slicer warns when configured nozzle temps fall below it. Printing under it risks underextrusion, poor layer bonding, extruder skipping.
nozzle_type: Nozzle material per extruder. hardened_steel and tungsten_carbide survive abrasive filaments (carbon- or glass-filled); stainless_steel and brass conduct heat better and suit plain polymers. Studio blocks abrasive filaments on brass.
nozzle_volume: Melt-zone volume (mm³) inside the hotend, per extruder. Sets how much filament must be purged to fully change colour or material.
only_one_wall_first_layer: Prints a single wall loop on the first layer instead of the full wall count. Gives bottom surface fill more area for a more uniform underside and can ease elephant foot; slightly reduces first-layer edge strength.
ooze_prevention: For multi-extruder printers: drops the idle extruder to a standby temperature so it oozes less while parked. Reduces blobs and color contamination; adds heat-up wait at each toolchange. Irrelevant on single-extruder machines.
outer_wall_acceleration: Acceleration (mm/s²) for outer wall lines. Lower reduces ringing/ghosting and corner artifacts on the visible surface at some time cost; raise for speed where cosmetics matter less. Typically the lowest acceleration in a profile.
outer_wall_jerk: Jerk / instantaneous speed-change limit (mm/s) for outer walls. Lower smooths direction changes, cutting ringing and corner bulge on visible surfaces; higher shortens print time. Typical 7-9; only applies when jerk control is active.
outer_wall_line_width: Line width (mm) for the outermost wall. 0 derives from the default line width. Narrower than inner walls sharpens detail and dimensional accuracy; wider improves strength and overhangs. Usually ~100-105% of nozzle diameter.
outer_wall_speed: Print speed (mm/s) for the outermost wall — the visible surface. Slowest of the wall speeds; lower improves surface finish and dimensional accuracy, higher saves time at cosmetic cost. Commonly 40-60% of inner wall speed.
overhang_1_4_speed: Wall speed (mm/s) for slight overhangs, 10-25% of line width unsupported. 0 keeps normal wall speed. Lower improves overhang surface; rarely needs slowing at this small a degree.
overhang_2_4_speed: Wall speed (mm/s) for moderate overhangs, 25-50% of line width unsupported. 0 keeps normal wall speed. Slowing here gives cooling time and reduces curling on the overhang edge.
overhang_3_4_speed: Wall speed (mm/s) for steep overhangs, 50-75% of line width unsupported. 0 keeps normal wall speed. Slow markedly (e.g. 10-25 mm/s) to prevent sag and curl; pair with raised overhang fan speed.
overhang_4_4_speed: Wall speed (mm/s) for extreme overhangs, 75-100% of line width unsupported. 0 keeps normal wall speed. Slowest overhang tier before fully floating lines; typically 10 mm/s territory with maximum part cooling.
overhang_fan_speed: Part-cooling fan speed (%) forced on overhang walls and bridges, overriding the normal min/max fan range. Higher freezes overhang lines faster, reducing sag and curl; for warp-prone high-temp materials (ABS) keep moderate. Default 100.
overhang_fan_threshold: Overhang ratio (per extruder position) above which the part-cooling fan is forced to its overhang speed. Expressed as line-width overhang percentage; 0% cools every line, 95% only near-bridges. Lower thresholds improve overhang surfaces on heat-sensitive materials like PLA; keep high for warp-prone ABS.
overhang_threshold_participating_cooling: Overhang ratio above which lines count toward layer-time cooling calculations (per extruder position). At 100% only bridges participate; lower values make overhanging lines trigger slowdown-for-cooling earlier. Tune together with overhang_fan_threshold.
overhang_totally_speed: Print speed (mm/s) for 100% unsupported (fully floating) overhang walls. Very slow so extruded lines can solidify mid-air; raising risks sagging and dropped loops. Default 10. Applies past the 75-100% overhang tier.
override_filament_scarf_seam_setting: Lets the process profile's scarf seam parameters replace those stored in the filament profile. Enable when tuning scarf seams per print regardless of filament defaults; off, filament-level scarf settings win.
override_process_overhang_speed: Lets this filament impose its own overhang speeds instead of the process profile's. Useful for materials needing distinct overhang handling (e.g. TPU, high-temp filaments); off, process overhang speeds apply.
physical_extruder_map: Maps each logical extruder to the physical extruder driving it. Identity on single-toolhead machines.
post_process: Shell commands run on the generated G-code after slicing, each receiving the G-code file path as final argument; scripts may modify the file in place. One command per entry; runs on the host machine at export time.
pre_start_fan_time: Seconds to issue the fan speed command ahead of an overhang or bridge region so the fan physically spins up before the lines print. Raise (up to 5 s) for fans with slow response; 0 changes fan speed exactly at the feature.
precise_outer_wall: Reduces overlap between outer wall and its inner neighbor so the outer wall's printed width stays exact. Improves XY dimensional accuracy and seam consistency; slightly weakens outer-to-inner wall bonding and adds a little print time.
precise_z_height: Adjusts the top layers' heights so total part height matches the model exactly instead of rounding to a layer-height multiple. Enable for parts with tight Z tolerances; final layers may print marginally thinner.
pressure_advance: Pressure advance coefficient for nozzle pressure lag: cuts corner bulge, seam blobs, gaps after travels. Typical 0.02-0.06 direct drive, higher for bowden or flexibles. Only active when pressure advance is enabled; calibrate per filament.
prime_tower_brim_width: Brim width (mm) around the prime tower for bed adhesion. Larger resists knock-over on tall multi-color prints at cost of material and plate space; -1 lets the slicer choose automatically. Default 3.
prime_tower_enable_framework: Adds internal rib structure inside the prime tower. Stiffens tall towers against wobble and collapse during fast purge moves; uses extra filament. Enable for tall prints with many filament changes.
prime_tower_extra_rib_length: Extends prime tower rib walls beyond the tower body (mm) for extra footprint and stability. Longer ribs resist tipping on tall towers; consume more filament and plate space. 0 keeps ribs flush. Requires rib wall enabled.
prime_tower_fillet_wall: Rounds the prime tower wall corners with fillets. Smoother corners keep tower printing stable at speed and reduce corner ringing on the tower; negligible cost. Default on.
prime_tower_flat_ironing: Applies a flattening/ironing pass on the prime tower surface so its top stays level despite uneven purge volumes. Keeps subsequent tower layers reliable; adds a little time per tower layer.
prime_tower_infill_gap: Gap between prime tower infill lines as percent of line width (min 100 = touching). Larger gap saves filament and speeds purging but weakens the tower; keep near default 150 for tall towers.
prime_tower_lift_height: Z-lift (mm) applied when the nozzle travels to the prime tower, avoiding drag across the print. -1 disables the extra lift. Raise if travels to the tower scar the part or hit curled edges.
prime_tower_lift_speed: Speed (mm/s) of the Z-lift move when traveling to the prime tower. Higher shortens the hop time but needs Z-axis speed headroom; the machine's Z limit caps it. Default 90.
prime_tower_max_speed: Speed cap (mm/s) for printing the prime tower. Lower improves purge line adhesion on the tower — important for flexibles and slippery materials; higher saves time on multi-color prints. Default 90.
prime_tower_rib_wall: Builds the prime tower wall with protruding ribs instead of a plain perimeter. Ribs widen the footprint and stiffen the tower against tipping; slightly more filament and plate space. Default on; pair with rib width/extra length.
prime_tower_rib_width: Width (mm) of the prime tower's rib walls. Wider ribs give a broader, more stable base for tall towers at cost of filament and plate space. Default 8. Only relevant with rib wall enabled.
prime_tower_skip_points: Omits the sharp rib tip points on the prime tower wall, trimming rib ends for cleaner, more reliable tower walls. Default on; disable only if full-length ribs are needed for maximum footprint.
prime_tower_width: Side length (mm) of the prime tower. Wider towers are more stable and absorb larger purge volumes per layer but consume plate space and filament. Min 2, default 35; increase for tall prints or many color changes.
print_extruder_id: Internal mapping of the print/process to a physical extruder (1-based), one entry per assignment. Managed by the slicer and object settings on multi-extruder machines; not normally hand-edited.
print_extruder_variant: Extruder/hotend variant tag the process profile targets, per extruder (e.g. 'Direct Drive Standard'). Selects which entry of variant-indexed vector settings applies. Profile-compatibility metadata; normally left as inherited, not hand-edited.
print_flow_ratio: Object-level flow multiplier stacked on the filament's flow ratio. >1 extrudes more (fills gaps, risks over-extrusion ridges); <1 less (cleaner surfaces, risks under-fill). 1 = neutral. Use for per-object tuning without editing the filament profile.
print_host: Hostname, IP address, or URL of the network print host g-code is uploaded to. Paired with host_type.
print_host_webui: URL of the print host's web interface. Convenience link only; no effect on slicing or upload.
print_in_clockwise: Prints perimeter loops clockwise rather than counter-clockwise. Changes which side the seam falls on and the direction overhangs are laid down.
print_sequence: Order for multiple objects. by layer: all objects advance together each layer — fastest, travels between objects can string. by object: finish each object before the next — cleaner parts, needs toolhead/gantry clearance around objects.
printable_area: Bed outline as a closed polygon of 'XxY' millimetre points, four corners for a rectangular bed. Bounds where objects may sit and fixes the origin all g-code coordinates are relative to.
printable_height: Highest Z (mm) the toolhead can reach. Objects taller than this cannot be sliced. Machine-specific; around 250 on most Bambu machines.
printer_extruder_id: Extruder index each printer_extruder_variant column belongs to. Lets one physical extruder carry several variants.
printer_extruder_variant: Active extruder variant per column, such as 'Direct Drive Standard'. Its length is the column count every per-extruder vector key in presets for this machine must match.
printer_model: Machine model this preset targets, such as 'Bambu Lab P1S'. Presets and filaments are matched to printers by this value.
printer_notes: Free-text notes stored with the machine preset. Ignored by slicing; useful for hardware mods and calibration history.
printer_structure: Motion system topology. corexy moves the head in XY on crossed belts while the bed drops; i3 moves the bed in Y; hbot uses a single H-shaped belt; delta uses three parallel arms. Determines which acceleration and jerk limits are realistic.
printer_technology: Printing process family this machine describes. FFF builds by extruding filament; SLA cures resin. Bambu Studio machine presets are FFF.
printer_variant: Hardware variant within printer_model, conventionally the nozzle diameter ('0.4'). Distinguishes one model's per-nozzle machine presets.
printhost_apikey: API key or password authenticating uploads to print_host. Blank when the host needs no credentials.
printhost_authorization_type: How print_host authenticates uploads. key: the single API key in printhost_apikey; user: printhost_user plus printhost_password.
printhost_cafile: Path to a CA certificate bundle used to validate the print host's HTTPS certificate. Blank uses the system trust store.
printhost_password: Password paired with printhost_user for user/password print-host authorization.
printhost_port: Printer identifier on the print host when that host serves several machines or queues.
printhost_ssl_ignore_revoke: Skips HTTPS certificate revocation checking when uploading to print_host. Reserve for intranet hosts whose certificates cannot be checked.
printhost_user: User name for print hosts using user/password authorization; see printhost_authorization_type.
printing_by_object_gcode: G-code inserted between objects when printing sequentially, after one object finishes and before the next starts.
process_notes: Free-text notes stored with the process profile. No effect on slicing or output.
raft_contact_distance: Z gap between raft top and the object's first layer. Larger = easier raft removal but rougher object bottom; 0 fuses raft to part. ~0.1 mm typical for PLA; only relevant when raft_layers > 0.
raft_expansion: Horizontal distance the raft extends beyond the object footprint (mm). More = larger adhesion area and stability against warping, at extra material and bed area. Default 1.5 mm.
raft_first_layer_density: Fill density of the raft's first (bed-contact) layer. Higher = stronger bed grip and stiffer base; lower = less material, faster. 90% typical; drop only if raft is hard to remove from the bed.
raft_first_layer_expansion: Extra horizontal expansion applied only to the raft's first layer beyond the raft outline (mm), enlarging bed contact against warping. -1 = auto (slicer-chosen). More = better adhesion, more material and bed area.
raft_layers: Number of raft layers under the object; 0 disables. Raft decouples part from bed — helps adhesion for warping materials and uneven beds, at cost of time, material, and bottom finish. Pair with raft_contact_distance for removability.
reduce_crossing_wall: Routes travel moves around perimeters instead of across them. Reduces stringing and surface scars from ooze without extra retraction; increases travel length and slicing time. Useful for oozy materials (PETG); off keeps travels direct and fast.
reduce_fan_stop_start_freq: Keeps the part-cooling fan spinning at low speed instead of fully stopping during brief fan-off spans. Avoids on/off cycling whose spin-up lag cools unevenly. Off for warp-prone materials needing zero fan.
