reduce_infill_retraction_mode: Retraction policy for travels inside sparse infill, where ooze stays hidden. Disabled: always retract. Enabled: skip retraction there — faster, less extruder wear, minor internal blobbing. Auto: slicer decides. Saves time on infill-heavy prints.
required_nozzle_HRC: Minimum nozzle hardness (Rockwell C) the filament demands, per filament. Nonzero for abrasives (carbon/glass fiber, glow) so the slicer can warn when the installed nozzle is softer, e.g. brass ~HRC 20 vs hardened steel ~HRC 55+. 0 = no requirement.
resolution: Path simplification tolerance in mm; geometry deviations below it are merged. Lower = more faithful curves but larger G-code and possible motion-planner stutter; higher = smaller files, visible faceting. 0.01 mm default rarely needs changing.
retract_before_wipe: Share of the retraction (percent) performed before the wipe move starts, per extruder. 100% retracts fully then wipes; lower values retract during the wipe, smearing less but oozing more.
retract_length_toolchange: Filament pulled back (mm) when switching to another extruder, per extruder. Longer than an ordinary retraction because the tip must clear the melt zone entirely.
retract_lift_above: Lowest Z (mm) at which z_hop applies, per extruder. Raise it to skip hopping on the first layers, where there is nothing to collide with.
retract_lift_below: Highest Z (mm) at which z_hop applies, per extruder. 0 means no upper bound.
retract_restart_extra: Extra filament (mm) pushed beyond the retraction when printing resumes, per extruder. Small positive values fight gaps after a retraction; too much blobs. Usually 0.
retract_restart_extra_toolchange: Extra filament (mm) pushed on restart after a toolchange retraction, per extruder. Compensates for material lost while the extruder stood idle.
retract_when_changing_layer: Retracts at every layer change, per extruder. Reduces the blob at the Z seam at the cost of one retraction per layer.
retraction_distances_when_cut: Distance (mm) pulled back during the cut retraction, per extruder. Must carry the tip past the cutter; 10-18 mm.
retraction_distances_when_ec: Retraction length (mm) when this filament is parked during an extruder change, per filament. Longer pulls filament further from the melt zone — less ooze while idle, but jam/slow-reprime risk if excessive. Multi-extruder machines only.
retraction_length: Filament pulled back (mm) on retraction, per extruder. Too little strings; too much grinds the filament and leaves gaps on restart. Direct drive 0.4-1.2 mm, bowden 2-6 mm.
retraction_minimum_travel: Shortest travel move (mm) that triggers a retraction, per extruder. Raising it skips retractions on short hops, saving time and filament grinding at some risk of stringing.
retraction_speed: Speed (mm/s) at which filament is pulled back, per extruder. Faster cuts oozing but risks grinding soft filament; 30-60 mm/s typical.
role_base_wipe_speed: Wipe move runs at the speed of the extrusion role it follows (outer wall wipe at outer-wall speed, etc.). Disable to control wipe speed independently via the wipe speed setting. Enabled default gives consistent seam wiping across features.
scan_first_layer: Runs the machine's first-layer inspection scan after layer one. Catches adhesion failures early at a small time cost.
scarf_angle_threshold: Corner angle (deg) above which a contour counts as smooth for smart scarf application. Scarf applied only on smoother contours; sharper corners keep a normal seam hidden in the corner. Lower = scarf used more often. Default 155.
seam_gap: Gap left at the end of a perimeter loop before the seam, as % of nozzle diameter. Larger = smaller seam blob but possible visible gap/weak spot; smaller = tighter joint, more bulge. 15% typical; reduce for dimension-critical or watertight parts.
seam_placement_away_from_overhangs: Shifts seams off overhang regions, where seam blobs curl and worsen surface defects. Experimental; can override the preferred seam position locally, making the seam line less consistent. Enable on overhang-heavy visual parts.
seam_position: Perimeter seam placement. nearest: closest point to previous loop — fastest. aligned: seams stacked into one vertical line — easy to hide or sand. back: at the model's rear (Y max). random: scattered per layer — no seam line, pinpricks all over.
seam_slope_conditional: Applies scarf seams only on smooth contours where a normal seam would show; sharp corners keep a regular seam that hides in the corner. Uses scarf_angle_threshold as the smoothness cutoff. Saves time versus scarfing everything.
seam_slope_entire_loop: Extends the scarf ramp around the entire perimeter loop instead of a short segment. Maximum seam concealment on round/organic shapes; adds print time and can soften Z dimensional crispness. Leave off for typical parts.
seam_slope_inner_walls: Applies scarf joints to inner walls as well as outer. Improves inter-wall consistency and can help strength/watertightness at seams; adds print time. Cosmetic-only goals need only external scarfs.
seam_slope_min_length: Length (mm) of the scarf seam ramp along the perimeter. Longer spreads the seam transition over more distance — less visible seam, slightly longer print. Default 10 mm; shorter on small perimeters where 10 mm would wrap too far.
seam_slope_steps: Number of discrete height steps in the scarf ramp. More steps = smoother slope and better seam blending, more G-code segments. Default 10; raising past ~10 gives diminishing returns.
seam_slope_type: Enables scarf joint seams: loop start/end ramp in Z so the seam overlaps gradually instead of butting. none: regular seams. external: outer walls only — hides visible seams. all: outer and inner walls. Costs time; tuned via seam_slope_* settings.
silent_mode: Declares that the machine offers a quiet motion mode running under its own, lower, machine limits.
single_extruder_multi_material: Declares that several filaments feed one nozzle, AMS-style. Enables purge and flush handling at filament changes.
skeleton_infill_density: Fill density of the skeleton (deep interior) zone when using a skin/skeleton-zoned sparse infill pattern. Lower saves material and time in the core; skin zone keeps its own density near surfaces. 15% typical.
skeleton_infill_line_width: Extrusion width (mm) for skeleton-zone infill lines in skin/skeleton-zoned patterns. Wider = stronger, faster core deposition with more material; keep near nozzle diameter (0.4 typical for 0.4 mm nozzle).
skin_infill_density: Fill density of the skin zone — infill adjacent to walls/surfaces — in skin/skeleton-zoned sparse infill patterns. Higher improves top-surface support and near-surface solidity without densifying the whole part. 15% default.
skin_infill_depth: Thickness (mm) of the skin infill zone measured inward from the model surface; interior beyond it becomes skeleton zone. Deeper = more of the part at skin density — stronger near surfaces, more material. Default 2 mm.
skin_infill_line_width: Extrusion width (mm) for skin-zone infill lines in skin/skeleton-zoned patterns. Wider = fewer, stronger lines near surfaces; narrower = finer support under top surfaces. Keep near nozzle diameter (0.4 typical).
skirt_distance: Gap (mm) between the skirt and the object outline. Larger keeps skirt clear of brims and easy to remove; smaller acts closer to a draft shield. Default 2 mm.
skirt_height: Skirt height in layers. 1 = normal priming skirt. Many layers builds a wall that blocks drafts around the part (draft-shield effect) — helps warp-prone materials without enclosure, costs material and time.
skirt_loops: Number of skirt loops around the print. Primes the nozzle to steady flow and previews bed adhesion/leveling before the part starts. 0 disables; 1-3 typical; more loops for small parts needing extra priming.
slice_closing_radius: Radius (mm) used to close cracks and pinholes in the mesh during slicing. Larger fixes leakier, non-manifold models but can seal intentional gaps and erase details smaller than the radius. Default 0.049 mm; raise only for broken meshes.
slicing_mode: Mesh interpretation. regular: inside/outside from face orientation. even_odd: even-odd fill rule — overlapping shells alternate solid/hollow (e.g. 3DLabPrint planes). close_holes: fills all enclosed cavities solid.
slow_down_for_layer_cooling: Enables automatic slowdown on layers finishing faster than slow_down_layer_time, letting each layer solidify before the next. Per filament. Essential for small parts in PLA/PETG; disable when slowdown causes heat soak or timing matters more.
slow_down_layer_time: Target minimum layer time (s), per filament. Faster layers get slowed (floor: slow_down_min_speed) so plastic cools before being covered. Higher = better small-feature quality, slower prints. PLA ~4-8 s; low for high-temp materials.
slow_down_min_speed: Speed floor (mm/s) for cooling slowdown, per filament. Layer-time slowdown never drops below this, preventing crawl speeds that cause heat soak, blobbing, and nozzle dwell marks. Default 10 mm/s; raise for heat-sensitive materials like PETG.
slowdown_end_acc: Acceleration limit (mm/s²) at the ending height of the height-range slowdown; interpolated from the start-height value as the print rises. Lower reduces ringing/wobble on tall slender prints. Default 100000 = effectively no limit.
slowdown_end_height: Upper end (mm) of the slow-down-by-height ramp. Speed/acceleration caps interpolate linearly from the starting-height values to the ending-height values between the two heights; above this Z the end values hold. Default 400.
slowdown_end_speed: Speed cap (mm/s) applied at slowdown_end_height. The ramp interpolates from slowdown_start_speed to this value; lower it to keep tall narrow prints slow near the top against wobble. 1000 = effectively no cap (feature off).
slowdown_start_acc: Acceleration cap (mm/s2) at slowdown_start_height for the slow-down-by-height ramp; interpolated toward the ending-height acceleration as Z rises. Lower to tame ringing/wobble on tall prints. 100000 = effectively uncapped.
slowdown_start_height: Z height (mm) where the slow-down-by-height ramp begins. Below it the starting speed/acceleration caps apply; between start and end height the caps interpolate linearly. Default 0 (ramp starts at the bed).
slowdown_start_speed: Speed cap (mm/s) at slowdown_start_height. With slowdown_end_speed defines a linear speed limit over Z, e.g. progressively slowing tall thin parts as height and sway grow. 1000 = effectively no cap.
small_perimeter_threshold: Size threshold (mm) below which a wall loop counts as a small perimeter and prints at small perimeter speed. Raise to slow more small loops (holes, pins, bosses) for roundness and cooling; 0 disables the classification.
smooth_coefficient: Transition-length control for smooth_speed_discontinuity_area. Lower value = longer, gentler speed ramps between wall regions, less banding on curved/overhang surfaces; higher = shorter, more abrupt transitions. Useful range ~1-200; default 80.
smooth_speed_discontinuity_area: Ramps outer-wall speed gradually where print speed would jump (e.g. entering overhang slowdown) instead of switching abruptly. Reduces gloss banding on curved surfaces; adds print time. No effect in spiral mode. Length set by smooth_coefficient.
solid_infill_filament: 1-based filament index used for internal solid infill; 0 = object's default filament. Only relevant on multi-filament setups; choosing a filament different from walls adds filament changes and purge waste every layer.
sparse_infill_density: Percent fill of the interior. Higher = stronger, stiffer, heavier, slower, more material; strength gains diminish above ~40% — extra walls are usually more effective. 0 = hollow, 100 = solid. Typical 10-25% decorative, 30-50% functional.
sparse_infill_filament: 1-based filament index for sparse infill; 0 = object's default. Interior is hidden, so a cheap filament works on multi-filament machines, but per-layer filament changes cost purge material and time.
sparse_infill_lattice_angle_1: First strut direction (degrees, -75 to 75) of the 2dlattice sparse infill pattern; default -45. Together with lattice angle 2 sets the crossing-strut geometry of lightweight wing/aero-style interiors. No effect with other patterns.
sparse_infill_lattice_angle_2: Second strut direction (degrees, -75 to 75) of the 2dlattice sparse infill pattern; default 45. Spread relative to lattice angle 1 controls cell shape; symmetric +/-45 is typical. No effect with other patterns.
sparse_infill_line_width: Extrusion width (mm) of sparse infill lines. Wider = fewer, thicker, stronger lines at the same density and steadier flow; narrower = finer lattice. Typically nozzle diameter up to ~125% of it; 0.4-0.45 for a 0.4 nozzle.
sparse_infill_pattern: Interior fill geometry. cubic/adaptivecubic/supportcubic: all-round strength, latter two densify near top only; grid/triangles/tri-hexagon: strong; gyroid/crosshatch: isotropic, flexible-friendly; honeycomb/3dhoneycomb: strong, slow; lightning: minimal, props top only; line/zig-zag/zigzag/alignedrectilinear: cheap directional; crosszag/lockedzag: zigzag variants; concentric: follows walls; hilbertcurve/archimedeanchords/octagramspiral: decorative; 2dlattice: struts per lattice angles. Default cubic.
sparse_infill_speed: Print speed (mm/s) for sparse infill. Interior is invisible, so usually the fastest feature; real limit is the filament's volumetric flow. Lower if infill lines break, rattle, or bond poorly to walls. Default 100.
spiral_mode: Vase mode: prints the outline as one continuous single wall while Z rises steadily — no layer seam. Forces 1 wall, 0 top layers, no infill or support above the solid bottom layers. Only for single non-overlapping vase-like solids.
spiral_mode_smooth: In spiral mode, additionally blends XY and Z over the loop start to erase the residual transition scar where the spiral begins, giving a fully seamless wall. Slight dimensional accuracy cost. Only active with spiral_mode.
standby_temperature_delta: Temperature offset (degC) applied to a filament's nozzle while it is inactive during multi-filament printing. Negative cools the idle extruder to cut oozing and stringing; larger drops add reheat wait on each swap back. Default -5.
supertack_plate_temp: Bed temperature (degC) after the first layer on the Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack, per filament. The plate grips at low temperatures: ~35 for PLA; 0 disables heating. Too hot causes elephant foot and over-adhesion; plate unsuited to high-temp materials.
supertack_plate_temp_initial_layer: First-layer bed temperature (degC) on the Bambu Cool Plate SuperTack, per filament. Usually equal to or slightly above the later-layer temperature; ~35 for PLA; 0 disables heating. Plate unsuited to high-temp materials.
support_air_filtration: Declares that the machine has an exhaust or filtration fan, enabling the filament keys that run it during and after printing.
support_angle: XY rotation (degrees, 0-359) of the support base pattern lines. Orient lines across the supported edge for sturdier support, or along the intended breakaway direction for easier removal. Default 0.
support_base_pattern: Fill pattern of the normal-support body. default: slicer picks per support style; rectilinear: parallel lines, easy removal; rectilinear-grid: crossing lines, stronger, harder to remove; honeycomb: strong, more material; lightning: sparse branching, fastest and leanest; hollow: perimeter only, no fill.
support_base_pattern_spacing: Line spacing (mm) of the support base pattern. Smaller = denser, sturdier support and better backing for interface layers, but more material/time and harder removal; 0 = solid. Default 2.5.
support_bottom_interface_spacing: Line spacing (mm) of bottom interface layers, where support stands on the model. 0 = solid interface. Wider spacing eases separating support from the model's upward-facing surfaces beneath it. Default 0.5.
support_bottom_z_distance: Vertical gap (mm) between a model top surface and support standing on it. Larger = easier removal, rougher contact patch on that surface; smaller = firmer stance, harder release. Usually ~1 layer height; default 0.2.
support_chamber_temp_control: Declares that the machine can hold a chamber temperature target, enabling chamber_temperature handling in filament presets.
support_cooling_filter: Declares that the machine has a cooling filter unit; prerequisite for cooling_filter_enabled.
support_critical_regions_only: Limits automatic supports to critical regions — slender overhang islands and cantilevers that would otherwise fail — skipping ordinary shallow overhangs. Saves material/time and cleanup; unsupported overhangs may droop slightly.
support_expansion: Horizontal offset (mm) applied to normal support outlines. Positive merges nearby regions and widens footprints for stability; negative shrinks contact away from adjacent walls to protect surfaces and ease removal. Default 0.
support_filament: 1-based filament index for support body and raft; 0 = current/default filament. Use a cheap filament here; reserve dedicated support material for interface layers via support_interface_filament with support_interface_not_for_body on.
support_interface_bottom_layers: Count of dense interface layers where support stands on the model. 0 = none (default), -1 = same as top interface count. Add 1-2 to protect the model's upward surfaces under supports, at some removal difficulty.
support_interface_filament: 1-based filament index for support interface layers; 0 = default. Dedicated support material (PVA, Support for PLA) permits zero top Z distance and near-perfect undersides; with normal filament, release relies on the Z gap.
support_interface_loop_pattern: Prints the topmost support interface layer as concentric loops instead of straight lines. Loops can follow curved contact outlines more continuously; straight lines (off, default) usually peel away more easily.
support_interface_not_for_body: Keeps the interface filament out of the support body: base prints with support_filament, only interface layers use the dedicated material. Saves expensive soluble/support filament. Disable to print whole supports with interface filament. Default on.
support_interface_pattern: Pattern of support interface layers. auto: slicer chooses per support type; rectilinear: parallel lines; concentric: loops following the contact outline; rectilinear_interlaced: line phase alternates between layers for denser coverage; grid: crossing lines, stronger but harder to remove.
support_interface_spacing: Line spacing (mm) of top interface layers. 0 = solid interface, smoothest supported underside; wider spacing saves material and eases removal at surface-quality cost. Default 0.5.
support_interface_speed: Print speed (mm/s) for support interface layers. Slower than the support body gives denser, more precise interfaces and smoother supported surfaces. Default 80.
support_interface_top_layers: Count of dense interface layers between support and the overhanging model surface. More layers = smoother underside but harder removal; 0 disables the interface entirely (rough surface, easy removal). Typical 2-3; default 3.
support_ironing_direction: Angle (degrees, 0-360) of ironing passes over the top support interface when support ironing is enabled. Set relative to the interface line direction to control the polished texture the model prints onto. Default 0.
support_ironing_flow: Extrusion flow during support ironing, percent of a normal layer. Just enough to fill grooves in the top interface and flatten the platform the model prints on; too high builds ridges instead of polish. Default 10.
support_ironing_inset: Margin (mm) kept from the interface edges during support ironing passes. Larger inset avoids dragging material over edges (blob risk) but leaves an unpolished rim near the boundary. Default 0.
support_ironing_pattern: Toolpath pattern for ironing passes over support tops. concentric: follows region outline inward, good for curved areas; zig-zag: parallel back-and-forth lines, faster and fine for flat pads. Only active when ironing is applied to supports.
support_ironing_spacing: Line spacing (mm) between ironing passes on support top surfaces. Smaller = smoother, flatter support interface and better overhang undersides, but longer print time. Typical 0.1 mm; rarely above 0.2.
support_ironing_speed: Speed (mm/s) of ironing passes over support tops. Slower gives the nozzle more time to flatten plastic for a smoother interface; faster saves time but irons less effectively. Typical 15-30 mm/s.
support_line_width: Extrusion width (mm) for support structures. Wider = stronger supports, harder removal; narrower = easier removal, less material, weaker towers. Near or slightly below nozzle diameter; 0 falls back to default line width.
support_object_first_layer_gap: Horizontal gap (mm) between support and object on the first layer only. Prevents support fusing to the part where both squish into the bed. Raise if first-layer supports weld to the model; 0.2 mm typical.
support_object_skip_flush: Lets the machine purge into an object already being printed instead of the wipe tower or chute during a filament change. Saves material where the object can absorb it.
support_object_xy_distance: Horizontal clearance (mm) between support walls and the object. Larger = easier removal, cleaner walls, weaker overhang edges; smaller = better support, more scarring. 0.35 mm typical; top_z_overrides_xy_distance can shrink it on slopes.
support_on_build_plate_only: Restricts support generation to structures rooted on the build plate; no supports standing on model surfaces. Avoids scars on the part but leaves internal or stacked overhangs unsupported. Useful with tree supports around organic shapes.
support_remove_small_overhang: Skips support for tiny overhang patches that print acceptably unsupported. Saves material and removal work; disable when every small overhang matters (e.g., mechanical faces, small horizontal holes needing support).
support_speed: Print speed (mm/s) for support bodies. Supports tolerate high speed since surface quality is irrelevant; raising cuts print time. Keep interface layers governed by their own speed. Typical 80-150 mm/s depending on machine.
support_style: Structure style. Normal supports: default = slicer picks; grid = rectilinear lattice, sturdy, harder removal; snug = hugs model outline, less material. Tree: tree_slim = thin branches, minimal contact; tree_strong = thick stable branches; tree_hybrid = trunks plus normal tops for flat overhangs; tree_organic = smooth curved branches.
support_threshold_angle: Overhang angle (deg from vertical wall) below which faces get support; larger value supports more geometry. 30 deg default; well-tuned printers often manage 45+ unsupported. Only applies to auto support types.
support_top_z_distance: Vertical gap (mm) between support interface and object underside. Larger = easier removal, rougher overhang bottom; smaller = smoother underside, fusing risk. Usually one layer height (0.2 mm); 0 for soluble interface filament.
support_type: Support generation mode. normal(auto): pillar supports wherever support_threshold_angle triggers; tree(auto): branching supports, less material and contact, suits organic shapes; normal(manual) / tree(manual): only where enforcers are painted or placed.
symmetric_infill_y_axis: Mirrors sparse infill toolpaths across the Y axis. Keeps infill patterns identical between a part and its mirrored copy, giving symmetric strength and appearance in paired parts. No effect on solid surfaces; off by default.
temperature_vitrification: Softening (glass transition) temperature (deg C) of the filament. Informational limit: parts deform above it, spools in a hot chamber or AMS can soften and jam. Drives chamber-temperature warnings, not a print control.
template_custom_gcode: Reusable custom g-code block shipped with the machine that a process preset can reference.
textured_plate_temp: Bed temperature (deg C) on the Textured PEI plate for layers after the first, per filament. Higher improves adhesion but can soften lower layers; lower eases release. Textured plates often need ~5-10 deg more than smooth plates.
textured_plate_temp_initial_layer: Bed temperature (deg C) on the Textured PEI plate for the first layer, per filament. Slightly higher than later layers aids initial adhesion into the texture; too high causes glossy squish and elephant foot. PLA ~45-65, PETG ~65-80 typical.
thick_bridges: Prints bridges as thick round-profile lines at increased flow instead of thin flat lines. Spans long gaps more reliably but leaves a rougher underside; off gives neater bottoms on short bridges. Interacts with bridge speed and flow.
thumbnail_size: Preview thumbnail dimensions embedded in the g-code, as 'WxH' pixels. Must match what the printer's screen expects.
time_lapse_gcode: G-code emitted once per layer to capture a timelapse frame, typically parking the head and triggering the camera.
timelapse_type: Timelapse capture mode. 0 (traditional): photos during normal printing, no extra moves, toolhead may appear in frame; 1 (smooth): toolhead parks each layer before the photo, clean frames, adds time, needs a prime tower for the extra extrusion.
top_area_threshold: Area-ratio threshold (%) governing which upward-facing regions qualify as top surfaces receiving top solid infill. Exact direction of effect undocumented. Default 200%; rarely changed.
top_color_penetration_layers: Layers a color painted on a top surface extends downward. More layers keep color solid through sanding or translucent filament but add filament changes. Default 4; multi-color prints only.
top_one_wall_type: Uses a single wall on top surfaces so solid infill reaches closer to the edge, improving top finish. not apply: disabled; all top: every layer with top surface; topmost: final layer only. Single wall slightly weakens edges.
top_shell_layers: Solid layers closing the top of the part. More hide infill show-through and pinholes, add strength and time; fewer save material. The stricter of this and top_shell_thickness wins. 4-5 layers typical at 0.2 mm.
top_shell_thickness: Minimum top solid thickness (mm). Slicer adds top layers beyond top_shell_layers until this thickness is met, keeping tops sound at small layer heights. 0 disables the thickness rule and only the layer count applies. 0.6-1.0 mm typical.
top_solid_infill_flow_ratio: Flow multiplier applied only to top surface lines. Slightly below 1 (e.g. 0.95-0.98) reduces over-extrusion ridges for a smoother top; too low opens gaps between lines. Tune after calibrating overall flow, not instead of it.
top_surface_acceleration: Acceleration (mm/s^2) for top surface extrusions. Lower than general print acceleration reduces ringing and corner bulges on the visible top; too low costs time. 500-2000 typical; null falls back to default acceleration.
top_surface_density: Line density (%) of top solid surface fill. 100% gives a closed, watertight-looking top; below 100 leaves intentional gaps between lines (rarely wanted except for texture effects or flexible parts). Keep 100 for normal prints.
top_surface_jerk: Jerk / junction deviation speed (mm/s) for top surface moves. Lower reduces ringing artifacts on the visible top at direction changes; too low causes blobbing at corners from deceleration dwell. Around 9 mm/s typical.
top_surface_line_width: Extrusion width (mm) for top solid surface lines. Narrower lines pack tighter for a finer, smoother top finish; wider fills faster with a coarser texture. Often set slightly below default line width, e.g. 0.4 mm with a 0.4 nozzle.
top_surface_pattern: Top solid surface pattern. monotonic: one sweep direction, uniform sheen, best default; zig-zag: rectilinear, can show joins; monotonicline: monotonic with connected ends; alignedrectilinear: same angle every layer; concentric: outline rings, suits round parts; hilbertcurve / archimedeanchords / octagramspiral: decorative, slower.
top_surface_speed: Print speed (mm/s) for top solid surfaces. Slower than internal solid infill gives cleaner, glossier tops with fewer gaps; the last visible layer rewards patience. 50-120 mm/s typical; nullable entries fall back to default speed.
top_z_overrides_xy_distance: Where support Z and XY distances conflict on sloped faces, honors top Z distance and lets the horizontal gap shrink below support_object_xy_distance. Better support of shallow slopes; possible side-wall scarring.
travel_acceleration: Acceleration (mm/s^2) for non-printing travel moves. Higher shortens travel time and reduces oozing/stringing windows; limited by machine rigidity, not print quality, since nothing is extruded. Often several thousand on CoreXY machines.
travel_jerk: Jerk / junction deviation speed (mm/s) for travel moves. Higher keeps travels fast through direction changes; excessive values cause skipped steps or frame resonance. Can exceed print jerk since no extrusion quality is at stake.
travel_short_distance_acceleration: Acceleration (mm/s^2) for short travel hops, e.g. between nearby infill lines. Lower than full travel acceleration cuts vibration and noise from rapid start-stop moves at negligible time cost. Null falls back to travel acceleration.
travel_speed: Speed (mm/s) of non-printing moves. Faster reduces print time and stringing (less ooze time over the part); limited by motion system, not quality. 120-500 mm/s depending on machine; nullable per-extruder entries fall back to default.
travel_speed_z: Speed (mm/s) of pure Z-axis travel moves (layer changes, z-hop). 0 uses the machine default / normal travel logic. Lead-screw Z axes need modest values (10-20 mm/s); too fast can stall Z steppers.
tree_support_branch_angle: Maximum tilt (deg from vertical) of tree support branches. Larger lets branches reach farther and root on the plate; slanted branches are weaker and can sag or break mid-print. 40 deg default; reduce for tall thin trees.
tree_support_branch_diameter: Diameter (mm) of tree support branches at the tip region. Thicker = sturdier, carries more overhang, more material; thinner removes cleaner. 5 mm default; branches thicken toward the base per branch diameter angle.
tree_support_branch_diameter_angle: Taper angle (deg) by which tree branches widen from tip toward base. Larger angle gives fatter, more stable trunks for tall supports at higher material cost; 0 keeps branches cylindrical. 5 deg default.
tree_support_branch_distance: Spacing (mm) between tree support branch contact points along supported overhangs. Lower = denser tips, better overhang surface, harder removal and more material; higher = sparser, easier removal, risk of sagging. Default 5.
tree_support_wall_count: Number of perimeter walls around tree support branches. -1 = auto (slicer picks per branch size); 0 = interface-less hollow branches, weakest; 1-2 = sturdier branches, slower and more material. Default -1.
upward_compatible_machine: Names of newer machine profiles that can also run prints sliced for this one. Lets Studio offer the job to a compatible printer.
use_firmware_retraction: Emits G10/G11 and lets the firmware retract using its own stored settings. The slicer's retraction lengths and speeds stop applying.
use_relative_e_distances: Emits extrusion-axis moves as relative distances (M83) rather than absolute (M82). Relative is the modern default and survives custom g-code that moves E on its own.
volumetric_speed_coefficients: Per-filament polynomial coefficients modeling max volumetric flow as a function of nozzle temperature. Filled automatically by flow-dynamics calibration; leave empty to use the flat filament_max_volumetric_speed limit. Not hand-edited.
wall_distribution_count: Arachne only. Number of walls, counted from the innermost, over which variable extrusion width is spread. 1 keeps outer walls at uniform width for best surface finish; higher values share width changes across more loops. Default 1.
wall_filament: Filament/extruder index used to print inner and outer walls in multi-material setups. 0 = follow the object's default filament. Match to infill_filament when hiding color changes matters.
wall_generator: Perimeter engine. classic: fixed-width loops, predictable flow, may leave gaps in thin features; arachne: variable-width loops that fill thin walls and gaps cleanly, fewer tiny gap-fill moves. Arachne default; classic if width variation causes artifacts.
wall_loops: Number of perimeter loops per layer. More loops = stronger, more watertight, slower, more material; strength gains beat raising infill density. 2 default; 3-4 for functional parts; combine with detect_thin_wall or Arachne for narrow features.
wall_sequence: Print order of wall loops. inner wall/outer wall: inner first, supports overhangs (default); outer wall/inner wall: best accuracy and surface, worse overhangs; inner-outer-inner wall: one inner, then outer, then rest — accuracy plus overhang support, needs 3+ loops.
wall_transition_angle: Arachne only. Geometric taper angle (deg) of a narrowing feature at which wall-count transitions stop being inserted; wedges sharper than this get no transition zone. Lower = fewer transitions, cleaner walls, possible tiny gaps in sharp tips. Default 10.
wall_transition_filter_deviation: Arachne only. Allowed extrusion-width deviation (% of nozzle diameter) before switching wall count, preventing rapid toggling between counts in slowly narrowing features. Higher = fewer transitions, steadier print, more width variation. Default 25%.
wall_transition_length: Arachne only. Length (% of nozzle diameter) over which the print blends when wall count changes in narrowing features. Longer = smoother flow ramp, less blobbing at transitions; shorter = crisper but more abrupt flow change. Default 100%.
wipe: Moves the nozzle along the path just printed while retracting, per extruder. Wipes the tip so less material oozes during travel; see wipe_distance and retract_before_wipe.
wipe_distance: Length (mm) of the wipe move, per extruder. Longer wipes clean the tip better but reheat the last extrusion; 1-3 mm typical.
wipe_speed: Speed of the nozzle wipe move during retraction, as % of travel speed (or absolute mm/s). Higher wipes faster with less ooze time but can smear; lower is gentler on soft surfaces. Only relevant with wipe enabled. Default 80%.
wipe_tower_no_sparse_layers: Experimental. Skips printing prime tower layers that contain no tool change; the tower resumes at the next change instead of adding sparse filler layers. Saves material and time; can destabilize tall towers and confuse Z alignment. Default off.
wrapping_detection_gcode: G-code run every wrapping_detection_layers layers to probe for filament clumping around the nozzle. Empty disables the check.
wrapping_detection_layers: Layers between clumping-detection probe checks. Lower checks more often at some time cost; 20 default.
wrapping_exclude_area: Bed region the clumping-detection probe must skip, as 'XxY' polygon points. Covers hardware the probe cannot touch.
xy_contour_compensation: Uniform XY offset (mm) applied to outer contours of each part. Positive grows parts, negative shrinks; use to correct measured dimensional error from extrusion squish. Holes are handled separately by xy_hole_compensation. Typical corrections within +/-0.1 mm. Default 0.
xy_hole_compensation: Uniform XY offset (mm) applied to holes. Positive enlarges hole diameter to counter the typical FDM hole shrinkage from corner cutting and squish; negative tightens. Independent of xy_contour_compensation. Typical values 0.05-0.2 mm for accurate bores. Default 0.
z_direction_outwall_speed_continuous: Experimental. Smooths outer wall speed changes between adjacent layers along Z so overhang-driven slowdowns ramp gradually instead of jumping, reducing visible banding at speed boundaries. Slightly longer print time. Default off.
z_hop: Height (mm) the nozzle lifts for travel after retracting, per extruder. Stops the tip dragging over printed material; costs time and can string. 0.2-0.4 mm typical, 0 disables.
z_hop_types: How the lift is performed, per extruder. Auto Lift lets the slicer choose per move; Normal Lift goes straight up then travels; Slope Lift climbs along the travel direction; Spiral Lift climbs helically, gentlest on the print. Slope and Spiral cost less time than Normal.
